source.title: Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: ...the impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The Sergeant-at-Arms is directed to make a proclamation.

turns.speaker: Alfredo Sotto Corpuz
turns.text: All persons are commanded to keep silent under pain of penalty while the impeachment court is in session for the trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte is hereby called to order. We shall be led in prayer by Senator Judge Alan Peter Cayetano.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: A reading from the book of Chronicles 2, 7, 14. If my people, who you are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sins and heal their land. Lord Father God, as we come to you here today, We acknowledge that before we are members of the prosecution or the defense, or before we are senator judges, or before we are those who are advocating the impeachment or the acquittal of the vice president, we are Filipinos. And even before we can say we are Filipinos, we are your children. So when you say, if your people, we ask Lord God that we be part of This verse, because you never lie, who says that if my people. We know, Lord God, that we call on your name. We know that we are humbling ourselves. We know that we pray. Yet, Lord, as a nation, have we really turned our back on our wicked ways? Even today, as we are nearing the wrapping up of this impeachment proceeding, Lord, nearing the conclusion. So many big cases, major cases of corruption remain silent. Cover-ups are happening left and right and corruption that has stopped may also be restarted. Next Monday, we will start looking at the national budget which could be a source of huge blessing to the Filipino people, a source of relief, a source of some medicine or cure for the economic woes of the country. But it could also be poison, Lord God, depending on what the deliberation, what the product of the deliberation will be. Lord, so as we humble ourselves to you today, we ask that we learn to look at ourselves first, our institutions, our intentions. Lord, again we ask that you make the evidence so, so, so clear, one way or the other. Very, very clear, Lord, and we ask that the objectivity Hit every single Filipino. Not only the senator judges but every Filipino. Make it very very clear whether conviction is in order or an acquittal. We pray for the integrity of the court, Lord God. The court has been through many trials, many debates, many Issues, Lord God. We leave this to your hands and to the judgment of history. But as we go on today, we pray, Lord God, that you will give us the strength, the wisdom, the patience, our Senate President, our leaders, the leaders of the House. Because even as we speak today, abortion is being discussed. And other great sins. So how can we ask you to heal our land unless we turn from our evil ways? Lord, teach us to turn from our evil ways. We lift this up to you in Jesus' mighty name. Amen.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: Amen. The Clerk of Court will now call the roll.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Roll call of members. Senator Judge Aquino. Senator Judge Cayetano, Alan. Senator Judge Cayetano, Pia. Senator Judge dela Rosa. Senator Judge Ejercito. Senator Judge Estrada. Senator Judge Go. Senator Judge Hontiveros.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Senator Judge Lacson. Senator Judge Lapid. Senator Judge Legarda. Senator Judge Marcoleta. Senator Judge Marcos. Senator Judge Padilla. Senator Judge Pangilinan. Senator Judge Sotto III. Senator Judge Tulfo, Erwin. Senator Judge Tulfo, Raffy. Senator Judge Villanueva. Senator Judge Villar, Camille. Senator Judge Villar, Mark. Senator Judge Zubiri. The Presiding Officer, Senator Judge Escudero. The Senate President, Senator Judge Gatchalian.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: With 16 senator judges present, the chair declares the presence of a quorum. In accordance with the rules of procedure on impeachment trials, the chair now recognizes the duly elected presiding officer to preside over the proceedings of the impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. Senate President. If there are no objections, we shall dispense with the reading of the journal, Journal No. 40 of November 11 and 12 of the Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, and consider it the same as approved.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The Clerk will please call the case before the Impeachment Court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Case number 004-2026, in the matter of Impeachment Trial, Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before asking for the appearances of the parties, the Chair would like to inform the parties that on the basis of the manifestation of the Counsel of Respondent regarding the witnesses they will present, the Court issued a subpoena. For the following witnesses, Attorney Rainer Dela Fuente, Dr. Ceferino Rodolfo, Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan, and Ms. Rowena Mendoza, all of which have been duly served through electronic mail. Also, Chair would like to inform the Senator Judges and the parties that in compliance with the request of Senator Judge Hontiveros during the trial of November 10, 2026, The Court on November 16, 2026 received a letter of City Accountant Vingeline Bahan with the following documents through electronic mail. Number 1, authority to travel dated November 13, 2025, issued by the City Mayor of Davao City authorizing her to travel to Beijing and Shanghai, China from December 2 to 7, 2025. And number 2, travel authority issued by the Department of Interior and Local Government in relation to that travel. The Clerk of Court is directed to furnish the Senator Judges and the parties with a copy of City Accountant Bahan's submission.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: With respect to witness Rowena Mendoza of the Center for International Trade Expositions and Missions, she acknowledged receipt of the subpoena but stated that she is presently in Frankfurt, Germany on an approved official mission on the Sabina Duces Tecum, CITEM is currently collating and gathering all relevant documents in relation to Cale88 Foods Corporation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: She does request for time to submit the required documents and to move the date of her appearance to a later date.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The chair shall act accordingly on her request before the end of today's trial, before we adjourn rather. or even before lunch so that she can act accordingly with respect not only to the subpoena at testificandum but also to the subpoena duces tecum. So ordered. Appearances of the parties.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Good morning, Your Honors. For the prosecution, we are ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: For the respondent.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Good morning, Your Honor. Same appearance for the respondent accused.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Who will handle Atty. Dela Fuente, Atty. Sheila?

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: We ask that Atty. Mark Vinluan be recognized, Your Honor. Atty. Mark Vinluan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Mark, for the prosecution who will handle the witness, Atty. Dela Fuente, Honorable Ridon.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: It will be Honorable Diokno, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Good morning, Honorable Chel. Call your

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: witness, Atty. Mark.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: Your Honor, but before calling the witness, the prosecution would like to get copies of all the documents which the four witnesses will be submitting. So that it can guide the cross-examination.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Have you provided them with a copy, Atty. Mark? Not yet?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We were given one set of documents earlier by the Senate staff, Your Honor. But at the proper time, we will furnish them with copies.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, kindly furnish them accordingly so that we will not delay with the cross-examination of the witness. You may call your witness, Atty. Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Morning, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: For the next witness, we call to the witness stand, Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly situate attorney Rainer to the witness stand.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The clerk is directed to place the witness on the road.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: Sir, kindly raise your right hand.

turns.speaker: Atty. Renato N. Bantug Jr.
turns.text: You, Rainer Dela Fuente, do swear that the evidence you shall give in the case now pending between the Philippines and Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte shall be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So help you God.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Dela Fuente, did you understand? Naunawaan niyo po ba yung inyong sinumpaan, kaugnay ng

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: inyong testimonya o pagbibigay na inyong testimonya sa umagang ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Can we address you as Atty. Rainer?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Sir. Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay, good morning, Atty. Rainer. Offer, Atty. Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Offer, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Number one, Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente is a certified public accountant, lawyer, and anti-money laundering compliance practitioner. Number two, his knowledge and experience will enlighten this honorable court of fundamental legal concepts related to the anti-money laundering law, thereby demonstrating that the findings of alleged unexplained wealth on the part of the Vice President, as well as the methodologies used therefore, are erroneous, malicious, and without merit. And number three, He will also testify on other relevant matters and identify documents. That would be all, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: We reserve the right to cross-examine, if Your Honor, please. Your Honor, I understand that the witness will be testifying on a curriculum vitae or resume. May we have a copy of that so that we can catch and follow while that's happening?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We will ask him about it, Your Honor, and we will... Provide the prosecution copies thereof.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: But I understand you only have one copy, counsel.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We asked... I think...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You have a copy. He has his own copy too.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: He has multiple copies, I believe.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You have multiple copies, Attorney Rainer, of the documents you will be presenting?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. It's in my USB. The electronic copies.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly submit it to the court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The OSAA is directed to get a copy of the USB so that we can print it and we shall... Make it available to the witness, Attorney Mark, in the course of his testimony. Pakikuha yung USB, please.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly give it to the secretary so they can print necessary copies.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: May we know, Your Honor, if there are other documents aside from the resume that were produced by the witness?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We will ask him if he provided or brought other documents. Can

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: we proceed now, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: What copies do you have, Honorable Chel? The CV?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I don't have... I thought

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: you were given copies already. What copies were given to them? Clerk of Court or Attorney Diokno?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I have three

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: documents, Your Honor, please. One is the profile of the witness. Second is an FATF report entitled Operational Issues. Financial Investigations Guidance dated June 2012 and the third is a paper authored by the witness among others entitled Financial Investigation and Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines to Tackle Wildlife and Environmental Crime in the Philippines dated July 2025.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We confirm that we also have the same set of documents.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay. Let's see how far we'll go. Kindly just bring it out, Honorable Diokno, whenever you want a copy and if the copy has not been given to you. You may proceed, Atty. Mark, with your direct examination of the witness.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Good morning, Atty. Dela Fuente. Good

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: morning, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Kamusta po kayo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay naman, Sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Okay naman. Alright, dumiretsyo na po tayo. The court issued a subpoena in relation to your appearance in today's proceeding. Naalala niyo po?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And then, we were just talking about it, but you brought Documents in relation to that subpoena, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, your honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Ilang sets of documents po yung dinalo nyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Three sets po, your honor. Electronic form.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. So, I'll just go through those documents.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, you brought a copy of your CV and then a copy of a publication entitled Financial Investigation and Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines. As well as a report, operational issues, financial investigations guidance.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Do you confirm this?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. I confirm those documents.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And may we confirm from the prosecution if those are the same set of documents that they have?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I have not seen the documents that he has. All I can say is that those were the documents provided to us by the court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: If copies of those documents are shown you, printed copies, you will be able to identify them.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: At this point, I'm showing you a copy. Can we use the court's copy, by the way, Your Honor, of the documents that he brought? I'm

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: sorry, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Can we use the court's copy

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: of the documents? Can he be provided with copies of those at this point?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: As well as any electronic form in a USB that was provided to the court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Are you referring to the CV and the first two attachments, Attorney Mark?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You have a copy, right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You have a copy, Honorable Chela?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: At this point, Your Honor, may we request, Your Honor, upon proper identification of witness of those documents that they be marked as our exhibits D-2-AML-1 and so on at the proper time, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So ordered.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. We are aware... And we also see in your CV that you are a certified public accountant. Can you share with all of us how or when you obtained your degree in accountancy?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I obtained my degree in accountancy from De La Salle University. So I have double degrees, Bachelor of Science in Applied Economics and Accountancy. I graduated October 2005, took the board exam 2006, passed the board 2006.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, and what school organizations were you part of, if any?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: During those times, the usual, I think, as far as I can remember, Junior Philippine Institute for Accountants and also Economics Organization for the school.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Very well. Now, after passing the board exam, what was your first experience as a certified public accountant?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: After passing the board exam, your honor, I went to law school. Same year, 2006, I entered San Beda College of Law.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: During that time, I'm a full-time student.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Until my third year, I applied with the Bureau of Internal Revenue as a revenue officer in Manila. I was a working student on my third year.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: That's around 2009.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2010. So that's my experience as a revenue officer. I was able to apply my knowledge on accountancy as a government employee.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Punta naman po tayo dun sa pagiging abogado ninyo. Kindly share with all of us when you obtained your law degree.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So I graduated 2011, took the 2012 bar exams, passed it. 2011, and then I took my oath 2012. And while waiting for the results of the bar exam, I applied with Punong Bayan and Aurelio as a senior tax associate. Then after the results of the bar exam, I went back to government service, was part of the pioneer batch for the governance commission for government-owned and controlled corporations, GCG. So,

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Your Honor, please, I'm very sorry to

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: interrupt the witness and the

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: defense counsel. But may I see clarification from the defense? Are they attempting to qualify this witness as an expert? Because there is nothing in the offer of testimony to that effect.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We will get there, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Then I will have to make an objection, Your Honor, because it's not part of the offer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: It's part of the offer, Your Honor. It's just couched in different terms, but we will talk.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: we'll talk about uh his expertise and his knowledge role

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: May I request a

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: ruling of the Honorable Court, Your Honor, please. I did not hear the word expert or being offered or qualified as an expert in the offer of testimony.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: While it was not specifically mentioned, Honorable Diokno, you can infer it from Offers 1 and 2. And it is also my understanding, given the...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Description of this witness when they requested for a subpoena that he is being presented as an expert in the particular field that he will be testifying to particularly, I guess, on AMLC matters.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Did you make an objection or made an observation, Honorable Diokno?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I made an objection, Your Honor, please.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: At this time, Honorable Diokno, I would have to overrule the objection. You may proceed, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Just a manifestation. Thank

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Attorney Diokno.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I'm very sorry, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Honorable Diokno, manifestation.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Just a manifestation that we are not admitting the credentials or qualifications of this witness and will include it in our cross-examination.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Duly noted. Subject to cross.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Pagkatapos ng law school and after passing the bar, what was your first experience as a law practitioner?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, again, as part of GCG, I started there as an Analyst for GOCCs. So there's an application, combined application of my knowledge in accountancy and also law. So that's under GCG.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So you mentioned that you have experience in government service. I understand that you are a former AMLC official. Please tell us about that experience.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sorry sir, what's the last part?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Former AMLC. Former AMLC official, please tell us about that experience.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. There's no basis yet. The witness has not testified that he was ever connected with the Anti-Money Laundering Council. We see that in the CV. But the witness has not identified the CV or attested to its truth, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly reform, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. We'll show you a copy of your own CV. Just so you can refer. It says in your CV that you are a former AMLC official. Can you please tell us more about that experience?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, I entered the AMLC in 2015 as a financial investigator, proper designation bank officer 2. So I was assigned with the compliance and investigation group during that time.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: All right. And what are your—what were your duties and responsibilities in relation to that role?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: uh well it's financial investigation we handle compliance matters financial investigation matters so any case referred to the council as part of the team that look into scrutinize check the data and produce reports that may be used by other

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: agencies, law enforcement agencies and other agencies with investigative powers.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: You mentioned the term financial investigation. Can you describe your duties as far as you can and responsibilities as such as a financial investigator?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: We start first, Your Honor, with investigative sparks, investigative triggers. There are cases referred to us and these cases are then assigned. Ina-assign ito sa iba't ibang grupo within AMLC Secretariat. At kami yung gumagawa from scratch up until case build up until makapag-produce ng report, investigation or report that may be used.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Number one, tulungan ang ating mga law enforcement agencies sa pag-iimbestiga sa predicate crime. And number two, if meron ng predicate crime, mag-proceed yun sa pag-file ng kaso for money laundering. So, in a nutshell, doon humiikot yung aking duty previously with the AMLC and during that time kasi magkasama ang compliance and investigation. So, other than pag-iimbestiga, yung routine compliance checks sa mga ating covered persons ginagawa rin doon base sa aking function dati-dati sa sekretaryat.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: How would you describe or how extensive is your experience in financial investigation?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, from 2015 to 2018, during that time, very small pa lang ho ang sekretariat so we really multitask. Lahat ho ng pwedeng iba tong trabaho, hindi ho namin pwedeng hindian yan. So ginagawa ho namin lahat.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Matanong ko lang po very quickly, kaya po ba gawin in two weeks ang isang extensive financial investigation?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Two weeks? Kaya, pero mahirap po. If we would be very realistic, kaya, pero sobrang hirap po yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Okay. We'll leave it at that, no? Kasi yung ibang so-called expert, two weeks lang. Now, let's move on. By the way, dito po sa profile nyo, napansin ko rin po na there's this term AML, CFT, and CPF compliance. Can you explain to us what these are?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. Ang anti-money laundering kasi ngayon hindi lang sa isa. Tatlo na sila. Mayroon ng terrorist financing at saka financing, rather, proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. So tatlo na yan. You cannot discuss money laundering without touching upon the topic on terrorism financing and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. So magkakasama na yung tatlo na yan. Paggamit ng ating financial system, in order to mask yung illicit sources of money. So yan ho ang mundo. So it concerns financial crimes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. How about this, you have also a role on regulatory advisory. Can you share your experience in this?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. When I left the public service po, ako ay pumunta sa private sector. I started a law firm with a friend and then later on, I branched out and started my own. 2021. That is AML Consulting PH. So aside from the private sector clients, I was also tapped by other government agencies as their AML consultant. Based on my competence and experience, tinulungan natin sila how to draft their own supervisory framework, how they will be governing their covered persons. So maganda ho kasi meron ang aking eksperyensya sa gobyerno dati na mix ko ho with my first-hand experience sa mga covered persons, private sector. So nakita ko ho kung saan nahihirapan ang ating private sector at napapaintindi ho natin sa kanila kung saan ang gagaling yung sa gobyerno. Bakit naghihigpit ang gobyerno? So sabi ko we have to be sa middle. We comply with the international standards but also we don't, for lack of better term, pahirapan itong ating private sector. So yung aking naging role, advisory lamang po, recommendatory. The ultimate decision maker are still kung sino yung head of the agency. So yan yung aking regulatory compliance work. We advise government agencies how to craft properly yung kanilang AML policy so that it is realistic. Hindi lang siya theoretical.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: With the permission of Attorney Mark and Attorney Rainer, continuing authority is given to assisting counsels to approach the witness at any point in time. And no further authorization need be given by the court nor the presiding officer. You may continue, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. You also have experience as an accredited trainer for the AMLC. Please tell us more about that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, I left the service in 2018. I had a one-year self-imposed bar na hindi ako nag-practice ng anything related to AML. So 2019, after one year, I applied for accreditation. I was one of the first three accredited trainers. So diyan ko sinimulan yung aking firm, training lamang. Hindi ko nga alam kung ito ay magpaprosper o hindi. So from time, yung aking mga nagiging estudyante, na niwala naman sila sa akin. So unti-unti dun ko na-build. Yung aking client base. They tapped me as their consultant. Kung ano yung tinuturo mo, sabi nila, tulungan mo kami how to craft our AML policies. So doon ho nag-expand yung aking practice. So dati-dati ho, mag-isa lang ako sa opisina. Ngayon ho, kahit papaano, meron na ho tayong mga team of lawyers, paralegals that do assist me in this kind of work. So from training, 2019, yan ho, hanggang ngayon ay tuloy-tuloy ko ho yung ginagawa. So covered persons, bangko, Real Estate, lahat ng tinatawag nating covered persons, we do provide training sa kanila.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, you also mentioned that you have your own consulting firm and according to your profile, you are the founder and lead counsel of AML Consulting PH. Can you tell us when this was organized and can you tell us your duties and responsibilities for this organization?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, yung AML Consulting PH, again, I started this 2021. Again, the focus po nito ay more, again, training, compliance work, and research. Our core, ano po namin sa training, again, later on, those that attended my sessions, they do tap yung ating hong opisina para kanila maging consultant kasi ito ay medyo technical. So they need assistance. Tinutulungan natin sila to craft their own MTPP, yung kanilang money laundering and terrorist financing prevention program, institutional risk assessment, post-registration compliance work. So ito, again, on the side lang kami, advisory. The ultimate decision maker remains the covered person. So ito ang ginagawa namin day in and day out. Sa dami ng ating covered persons, in my own way, nasa private sector, Masaya rin ako kasi natutulungan ko rin yung aking mga dating kasamahan sa AMLC. Tinuturuan natin ng tama, hindi tinuturuan ng mali yung mga covered persons.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. You mentioned that you also work for the BIR or the Bureau of Internal Revenue. Can you share with us that experience as well?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. Your Honor, noong 2009 to 2010, For at least one year, I worked with Revenue Region 6, BIR Manila, as a revenue officer. So, I was part of the assessment group. So, we review tax dockets na inaakyat po sa Revenue Region 6, Manila. So, pagre-review ng mga assessments, lahat po ng taxes, business taxes, income taxes, before... I-close yung case or pag may kulang pa, binabalik ko namin sa mga revenue district offices or sa RDOs.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, you also mentioned governance commission for government-owned and controlled corporations. This is under the office of the President, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And can you tell us your experience on this? What were your duties and experience, your responsibilities, as well as knowledge and trainings that you gained?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, so for this one, Your Honor,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2012. I entered this commission as a financial analyst and then later on I was transferred to the transportation and infrastructure sector. So lahat ito, mga GOCCs na nandoon sa sector na iyon, in-evaluate po namin ang kanyang financials. Kailangan bang itong i-rationalize?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: i-close, i-dissolve yung mga korporasyon na ito? Kami yung gumagawa ng analysis and we give recommendations sa aming commissioners as to what are our findings and ano yung mga recommendations para matulungan yung ating gobyerno, lalo na sa mga GOCCs na hindi na based on their mandate.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: You were also an accredited trainer for the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation or PAGCOR. Can you please tell us more about that?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: After getting my 2019 accreditation from the AMLC, nagkaroon ko ng accreditation process ang PAGCOR for the casino sector. So I was fortunate enough to be the first accredited AML trainer for the casino sector. So as far as I can remember, around 2022 or 2023.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And what were your duties and responsibilities?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yung ating mga PAGCOR covered entities, casinos, land-based and internet-based casinos, they are required to undergo training. Again, we expect them to have these AML measures in place for the board and the frontliners to, again, properly implement it. They need proper training. So ito ang ating nagiging role. During that time, I think,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Marami ho kasi sila. So, in a way, it is being outsourced by PAGCOR to us through an accreditation process. So, I took the chance po of having this to complement my AMLC accreditation.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. You also have experience as an independent consultant at the AML Research Center Asia Pacific or RCAP Incorporated. Please tell us more about your role in that organization.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ito ang AML Research Center Asia-Pacific. This is an independent research firm. We registered this here in the Philippines. Hindi ako technically kasama sa grupo na ito. Ang purpose nito, kasi lumalaki na ang practice, is to detach it from AML consulting and have it dito sa research center na ito. More on collaborating. With other international bodies. Kasi over the years, I noticed na nare-recognize na rin ang Pilipinas pagdating sa AML matters. So nakakatawa nga po, mayroon na mga US-based fintech companies that do contact us asking for independent AML. Compliance Testing. So to delineate yung role domestic sa international, ito yung research center for this one and I am also designated here as a senior technical official po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, you mentioned yung independent consultant. Matanong ko lang sir, kapag sinabi po bang independent, do you weigh both sides or just focus on one side?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I think you don't take sides po. That will destroy your independence. So your findings might go against the institution that engage you. So you're only answerable dun sa standards that you apply as a consultant.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Bakit po? Pag-focus po ba kayo sa one side, ano po bang effect dun sa independence niyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, again, there are biases.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: It obscures your overview from the start. So again, it derails your work. There is a bias.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: You also have experience as a former consultant for CEZA. Para lang po alam ng lahat ano po ba tong CEZA and what were your duties and responsibilities dito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yung CEZA po, Cagayan Economic Zone Authority. If I may correct your honor, consultant pa rin po ako nila.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Up to now.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Sorry for that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes. So ang CEZA po kasi one of our supervising agencies and so far as AML matters. So again, as their advisor pagdating mo sa AML matters in crafting their supervisory framework, they are considered a supervisor po sa AML matters for their covered persons.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: CEZA covered persons that are under the AML regime. So doon sa aspeto na iyon, sa segment na iyon, doon tayo tumutulong. Crafty, the framework.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt the defense and the witness. But may I know the relevance of this line of questioning? The witness apparently is delivering his credentials on anti-money laundering. But the respondent in this case is not being charged with any money laundering crimes. The issue before this court are all centered on unexplained wealth, non-declaration of SALN, and participation in business. And I haven't heard anything from this witness that would qualify him on those matters.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Attorney Mark, what do you say?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: I have to correct the good counsel. Under the articles of impeachment, there are actually allegations pertaining to money laundering and other related matters. So, we will tackle that issue later on, Your Honor. But in the meantime, Your Honor, can we just proceed with qualifying this?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: At any rate,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, they presented an AML...

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: If I may be allowed to finish...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: In fact,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, they presented an AMLC witness. and they made interpretations on the data as well. They also presented their own witness, Your Honor. So, it is our position that, Your Honor, that we also have the prerogative to present our own expert on the witness.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: May I speak, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Honorable Diokno.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Well, I would have to most respectfully disagree with the attempt by the Defense Council to correct this representation.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I have seen and read the articles of impeachment a number of times. I have not seen any single word that refers to the respondent committing any crime under money laundering. So may I know where in the articles that is contained, if any? Because an

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: allegation like that is too serious to let pass.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: i hope that i will count you to it the council that you will show it at the

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: The point you decide to.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Very well, Your Honor. Can

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: we just move on?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: To abbreviate the proceedings, Honorable Chel, that Attorney Rainer is qualified as an expert by the counsel for respondent, Attorney Mark, only means that he can give his opinion. Not that it's gospel truth, not that it's the truth, not that it's accurate, not that it's correct, but only to allow the witness to give his opinion if he's qualified as an expert.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: He will be testifying to giving his opinion on documents identified, AMLC documents identified, presented, offered, and allowed by this court. So, in the interest of abbreviating the proceedings, again, subject to cross, of course, as regards the depth of his expertise. It will only, qualifying attorney Rainer as an expert will merely Enable him to give his opinion. Not that it's correct, again, not that we agree with it, not that it's legal, not that it's accurate, but only to give his opinion. As opposed to an ordinary witness that's not allowed to give his opinion.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So, we can skip with this if you will stipulate that he is an expert that can give his opinion with respect to AMLC documents identified by the prosecution and by the defense. Correct, Attorney Mark?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: By the defense also.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: That's correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Or if you don't want to concede it, you're also free to do so, Honorable Diokno. And we can proceed with... I think we're about to go to the seminars he has attended.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We're going to that.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: If Your Honor, please.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Honorable Diokno.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I was questioning the relevance of the line of questioning of the Good Counsel. He responded by saying that it is relevant, but said that... The reason being that money laundering is included in the articles of impeachment, particularly Article 2. Since that is his contention, Your Honor, please may we hold him to that now and may we ask him to show the relevance of this line of questioning by pointing to the allegations of the Article 2 that according to him pertain to money laundering.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor, we will cite the exact page later on but it will preempt our line of questions, Your Honor. We ask for some leave with your honor. And besides,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Honorable Diokno, again, you have common exhibits coming from AMLC by both the defendant and the prosecution, which is the proper subject matter of this witness to testify on. Again, if he is going to be qualified as an expert. May the court ask again, are you willing to stipulate as to his...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Expertise on the subject matter. Again, Honorable Diokno, without conceding that what he will say will be the truth and is accurate and is legal and correct. Subject to cross.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Inasmuch as I would like to facilitate the proceedings, Your Honor, I am not in a position to make any such stipulation at this point.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Then we will listen to the seminars he attended.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Very well, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Attorney Mark, you may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Let's move on. Sorry for that interruption, Attorney Dela Fuente. You also worked for APECO. Can you tell us more about APECO and your duties and responsibilities with this organization?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: For APECO, your honor, Aurora Pacific Economic Zone Authority, same with CEZA. They have the same requirement during that time, crafting their supervisory framework, helping them how to perform their function, forming their own AML department. So, yan ang aking naging role sa kanila, setting up their AML group. So, I think it's for only one year or one and a half year lang po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. By the way, what other accountancy associations or institutions are you affiliated with? And what are your roles and positions in these associations or institutions, if any?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As a CPA, we're part of the Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants. And from time to time, when I ventured into AML practice, they do invite me as their resource speaker or subject matter expert for AML. Kasi ang profession ng CPAs ngayon, covered na rin ng AMLA. So pagdating sa ganitong mga sessions, ako ang nagpa-facilitate.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. What other law-related associations or institutions are you affiliated with and what are your roles and positions in such associations or institutions, if any?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Currently, Your Honor, sa IBP. I have yet to be invited by IBP for AML-related trainings. But other associations, yung ating mga covered persons. Sa mga banko, RBAP, Rural Bankers Association of the Philippines, they have invited me to speak before them for AML matters. Association po ng mga non-bank financial institutions, yung PAFERA, Philippine Association for Foreign Exchange Dealers and Remittance Agents. Sa real estate din ho, yung SHDA, Subdivision in Housing Development Association. So they do top me as their resource speaker pagdating sa mga ganitong AML matters.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Marami na po tayong na-discuss na roles niyo sa education and professional experience as well. But what awards and citations can you share with us, if any?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, individual awards, Your Honor. Wala ho. Kasi nung ako ay nasa gobyerno na Agency-based awards. But when I ventured into private sector, again, ito kung when they do invite me as their resource speaker, Arbap, Seda, local and international, those recognitions ang binavalyo ko po the most. So it's not the trophies but the recognition about my competence and experience that what matters to me po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, thank you for that. Meron pa po ba kayong any significant role or na hindi pa natin natalakay? Or any organization that you are part of?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: More or less, yun na po yun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: More or less, Your Honor, yun na po. Lately, dun 2025 po, I was invited by an international organization, a non-profit organization, Traffic International, to help them in coming up with a paper. Using financial investigation in tackling illegal wildlife trade or environmental crimes. So it started with a research paper and then later on that research paper, naging libro po and we use it to train law enforcement agencies here in the Philippines and also the private sector to combat illegal wildlife trade. So nung hung nag-start siya 2024, 2025, we did a trading caravan and this year po. Meron kami noong April and next week meron kami noong November. So it will involve the public and private sector.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. So you mentioned that you are an author. Can you tell us about your participation in the publication of this book that you brought, Anti-Money Laundering Handbook? Can you please, very briefly, can you please tell us what this book is all about? And also ask my assisting counsel to make him identify it.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. So, Your Honor, last July of 2025, we were able to come up with this practical handbook entitled Financial Investigation and Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines to Tackle Wildlife and Environmental Crime in the Philippines. So I am—I was the lead author, with me Mr. Ben Brock and Mr. Serene Chng.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: This book is supported by the US Department of State and Bureau of International Narcotics and The purpose is to give a practical handbook sa ating hong Philippine law enforcement agencies so far as doing their financial investigations. So I use my experience in crafting this. The purpose is to adopt follow the money principles in conducting investigations. Hindi ko kasi matitigil ang ganito mga krimen kung hindi natin

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Pipigilan yung pera. Yun ang source ng motivation why these crimes still proliferate and we hit the criminals where it hurts them the most. Dito ay sa kanilang financial aspect. Ang purpose nito is not to compel or force law enforcement agencies to adopt whatever is on this book but to give them an insight. Ano ba ang best practices na ginagawa?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: ng ating financial intelligence unit, ng ating financial investigator, which is the AMLC, pagdating po sa mga ganitong krimen.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: At this point, Your Honor, may we request that the court's copy of this document be marked as our exhibit accordingly, considering that he already identified the same in open court at the proper time.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: So marked.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: All right. There is another publication here entitled Operational Issues, Financial Investigations Guidance. Can you tell us what

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your role is or how you use this in your practice?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. Your Honor, ito pong FATF report dated June of 2012 entitled Operational Issues on Financial Investigations Guidance. Ito yung aming ginagamit insofar nung ako ay ginagawa ang libro na ito. Ito ang aking naging basis in aligning. Itong libro na ito, with the internationally accepted standards, which is again promulgated by the Financial Action Task Force, FATF. Again, hindi ho ito yung strict rules, but these are merely recommendations, guidance, from the international bodies setting the standards to combat money laundering. So we aligned the book with this FATF report.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: It's entitled Regulatory Issues No. 2. Can you share us more about this? and so far as your goal that you discussed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, ito kong makapal na dokumento composed of 200 pages. We call this the GoTRACS. Ito ho ay ang Guidelines on Transaction Reporting and Compliance Submission. It was, again, Regulations No. 2 Series of 2024. Ito ho yung mga regulasyon. Sa pagre-report, pagsasubmit ng mga covered and suspicious transaction reports sa ating AMLC. Akin lamang po itong sinama sa aking submission kasi ito yung ating magiging basis later on kung ang tanong ay mapunta sa pag-interpret ko ng mga CTRs and STRs. Ito yung governing rule right now.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: At this point, Your Honor, we also request that the documents identified by the witness also be marked accordingly at the proper time. All right. Maraming salamat, Atty. Dela Fuente. You've already shared a lot about your educational and professional background. But please tell us, what is your passion with regard to your accountancy and law practice?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, nung hong ako ay nasa accountancy practice talaga, tax. Huwag na talaga ang aking

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Focus. That's the reason why I applied with the Bureau of Internal Revenue to gain knowledge, apply my tax, gain real world tax experience, how to audit. Pagdating naman sa aking law practice, again, hindi ko hupilano kung saan ako dadalhin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Nakapunta ako sa AMLC Secretariat and yung aking trabaho doon lumapit na sa aking puso. Yun na ang naging advocacy ko.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Hindi ko rin inakala na dito ako dadalhin sa ganitong klaseng practice. Dito kasi sa

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ito ang AML practice. So I tried to focus on this one.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you. What is your hope in terms of uplifting the accountancy and legal profession?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, number one po ano, ito hung AML practice again. Ngayon ho, just sharing, sa

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa aming opisina, meron na rin mga eskwelahan, ating mga top schools and state universities and colleges na nagbibigay ng partner kami sa kanila to give internship program. So we expose them na meron another opportunity and that is AML practice. So

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: by sharing this with students, future lawyers, future accountants, we are giving them Opening to them new opportunities for practice that they can apply here or even gain employment abroad. And while doing that, we also instill to them integrity and independence.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you po for generously sharing your background, Atty. Dela Fuente. Now, please allow us to ask, what political affiliations do you have, if any?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: None, Your Honor. Unfortunately, starting

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2019, hindi na ako nakaboto.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And to obviate the need of any cross-examination on this point, let me just ask you a more pointed question. What is your personal or professional affiliation with the Vice President, if any?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Mark, your turn. You may proceed with your direct examination or rather continue with your direct examination of Atty. Rainer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Atty. Dela Fuente, let me direct your attention to Section 8A of the AMLA. You already mentioned this a while ago but I'll read it for the benefit of the Senator, Judges, and the public. Information security and confidentiality states that, and I quote, the AMLC and its secretariat shall securely protect information received or processed and shall not reveal in any manner any information known to them by reason of their office. This prohibition shall apply even after their separation from the AMLC. You were part of the AMLC Secretariat. Please describe the powers and limitations of this office in terms of revealing confidential information.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, Your Honor, this is one of the, there are three rules on confidentiality and this is the third rule found on the first paragraph of 8-A. Now, it admits of an exemption on the second paragraph that is for authorized disclosure if this pursuant to information exchange. and if it is pursuant to an order of a court of competent jurisdiction. Now, again, the rule is that there is confidentiality should be the followed exception, again, if it is pursuant to information exchange and also pursuant to an order of a lawful court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. What types of data? and information are considered confidential information under this provision.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So confidential information here would cover the transaction reports, CTRs and STRs, derivatives of these CTRs and STRs. So that would be the intelligence reports and the investigation reports.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And to be sure, how strict must the AMLC be with the rule on confidentiality?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So again, under the same section, second paragraph,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Paragraph allowing for the disclosure. It says there that the AMLC shall formulate rules concerning information security, confidentiality, procedures for the proper handling, protection, storage of the information. So there are still safeguards. It is authorized but controlled disclosure.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Pertinent AMLC reports in this case contain a portion indicating general principles of information exchange with regard to the end user of confidential information from the AMLC. We don't want to flash the document on the screen, so I'll just go through the points one by one. We'll just get your comments thereon. Number one is, what does it mean? that the end user must first verify the information provided.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, again, this is... Again, this is still subject to the verification of the end user. So, again, the report does not contain conclusions but rather intelligence information. So, again, it is up to the end user as to how they will appreciate the information.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, so in your experience po as a financial investigator, paano po ba ginagawa yung tamang pag-verify ng information contained in these reports?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well again, the end user of the report, normally it's a law enforcement agency or an agency with investigative powers. There are things that are outside the... The view of AMLC. Again, money laundering lang sila. But dun sa unlawful activity, it's within the powers of the investigating unit, the law enforcement agencies. So again, some information might not have been disclosed sa AMLC. So it's up to the end user to verify if this information is useful or not.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Number two, what does it mean that the end user must protect the confidentiality of the information?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, since this information are, again, subject to verification, if it falls in the hands of, again, an unauthorized individual or organization, it might be used. It may deviate from its intended use or purpose. So we have to protect its confidentiality. It's subject, again, to verification. Subject to further checking by the end user.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Ano po ba yung tamang measures para masiguradong mapoprotektahan yung confidentiality ng mga impormasyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Number one po, ano? Depende po yan sa ilalagay ni AMLA. Kasi there are, again, different information that should be handled. Wala pong isang rule lang for every information. So normally, It should be restricted to the end user. The use should only be confined to the intended use indicated in the report.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, and proceed po tayo sa number 3. What does it mean that the end user must use the information for intelligence purposes only?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay, when we say for intelligence purpose only, it is for analytical purpose. Not

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: for evidence gathering or leading to coercive measures. For case build-up, for information gathering.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. How proper po na i-disclose yung mga datos sa publiko kung wala naman pong court order?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Very dangerous po ito if we let this out in the public. Why? Because we are in fact compromising the safety and security of the concerned account holder, the

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: covered person, and also the one who processed the information.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you. Number four, last two na lang po. What does it mean that the end user must not use information as evidence in formal proceedings?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: For number four,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor, again,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: it is not the evidence. It is not the... Evidence itself. Yan ho ay for intelligence use only. Para ho siyang nagbibigay ng clues, investigative leads. It doesn't give you the exact evidence but it leads you. Tinuturo niya kung saan ang mga ebidensya. Leads

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: lang ho ito. Parang clues. Nagbibigay ho ng clues.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Ano po ba yung mga formal proceedings contemplated under this rule?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: When we say my own appreciation po of formal proceedings, that would These are coercive proceedings, court proceedings, one that would involve appreciation of the facts and also a ruling, an order from a court of competent jurisdiction.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, and finally, what does it mean that the end-user must refrain from reproducing, copying, extracting, printing, or distributing material to any third party without the written consent of the council members?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So I think your honor, it's self-explanatory. No forward dissemination. No re-dissemination from its intended user cannot go beyond those who are originally the intended end user. So it cannot be re-forwarded, it cannot be re-disseminated.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Now, my next question is this. What is the legal effect? Confidential data and information on VP Sara and Attorney Manz being disclosed in a public proceeding similar to what happened in the House Committee on Justice on April 22, 2026.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Your Honor, objection. The question is misleading. The documents produced by the AMLA before the Committee on Justice were based on a subpoena issued by the Committee. That should be clear.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Subject to that qualification. Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: I'll repeat, ano pong legal effect kapag ang confidential data or information po ni VP Sara and Attorney Mans were disclosed in a public proceeding similar to what happened in the House Committee on Justice on April 22, 2026, subject po dun sa qualification na sinabi ni Representative Diokno, na sinabi na po yun, but with the added qualification na hindi po sila court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, Your Honor, I have no personal knowledge as to the matter surrounding that scenario. But what I can relay, Your Honor, nasa Section 14D, if

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: there is a violation of confidentiality, there is a corresponding criminal liability to those who violated that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Now, just to ask another point on this, who will you consider po as end users? Of confidential information kapag ginawa na pong public yung hearing, for example.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Kapag ginawa ng public.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Kanyari, public na po yung hearing, since public po yung hearing and televised, who will you consider as the end users ng mga confidential information kapag gano'n?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, it doesn't convert the information from being confidential to now a unclassified information or a freely available information.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The confidentiality nature of the information still remains with that data.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Now, based on your knowledge also as a financial investigator, ano po ba yung mga measures na can be used or observed when end-users receive confidential information in a public hearing, for example, like the one before the House Committee on Justice?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor, like the one flashed on the screen. A while ago, those are just some of the measures na nilalagay ko dun sa mga reports emanating from our AMLC. So that would restrict use of the information to only the intended users and will serve as a caution, as a reminder to those who might be accessing it without proper authority.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Let me direct your attention to section 14. You mentioned this, but I will no longer read. I will be more circumspect this time. But it talks about breach of information, security, and confidentiality. Itanong ko lang po sa inyo, as an expert on this matter, who are the responsible persons in case of breach of information, security, and confidentiality?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. There's been no finding that this witness is an expert and that the subject of dispute.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: If he knows, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I object to the qualification of the witness or the statement describing him as an expert. I move to strike that portion.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: If he knows, counsel, in regard to the qualification or description as an expert, let it stay on the record, subject to cross with respect to his qualifications. Witness, may answer?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor, under Section 14D, as to who will be liable, again, the one, I think, the one here, po, no? Who access without authority The confidential information. So that's the first one. Second, if the offender is a public officer or employee, there is a corresponding accessory penalty. And third, if it is disseminated or disclosed by the mass media, and then it will also include the reporter, publisher, editor-in-chief, and as indicated under Section 14D.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: All right. Tuloy lang po natin sa paragraph F. Nakalagay doon imposition of administrative sanctions. Again, I won't read the entire provision but based on this provision po and based on your experience with AMLA also, what are the natures of the penalties involved po sa batas? Aside from those that you already mentioned.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa administrative sanctions mo under section 14, normally it includes monetary and non-monetary penalties. So it can range from a simple reprimand up to imposition of monetary penalties as high as 500,000 Philippine pesos per violation.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, so you mentioned media. So it will be a teaching moment for all of us as well. Based on your knowledge and experience as a financial investigator, how should the media handle confidential information as end users?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As much as possible, it must be again in line with AMLA and our law on data privacy. Sensitive personal information should be redacted, removed, or blocked. So that it cannot reveal this information. It can be used weaponized against the account holder.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Let's go back to Section 7.1 of the AMLA. And I'll read, To investigate suspicious transactions and covert transactions deemed suspicious after determination by AMLC, money laundering activities, and other violations of this Act. So based on this provision, please describe to us. The process how the AMLC must conduct financial investigation based on CTRs and STRs. I-detail yun na

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: po natin. Where does the investigation process begin?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Okay. When we say investigation, that’s already stage two. Prior to investigation, we have what we call financial intelligence. That’s stage one. So day-to-day, the AMLC receives, analyzes, and disseminates this financial intelligence information. So it can be again forwarded to law enforcement or its own financial investigation group.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: If there is already a predicate crime, saka na po siya pupunta sa second stage, financial investigation. The first one, stage one, financial intelligence is more on the analytical part. Analysis lang ho yan. Second part, that is the more coercive evidence gathering phase. That is the financial investigation stage. Now before mag-proceed ho sa ating mga coercive processes, there must be an AMLC, well, council authority. So that would pave the way for filing for a petition, for freeze order, bank inquiry. Civil Forfeiture. So, provided po siya ng Section 10, 11, and 12 ng ating AMLA.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. You mentioned yung referral to law enforcement agencies. Ano po ba yung mga measures that the AMLC observes in relation to this stage of the process?

turns.text: And we very much appreciate, Your Honor, the leeway that has been given to us. But just to answer the question of the presiding officer, there's a couple pages worth of questions, Ron.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Just one follow-up question on that.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly turn on the mic of Senator Judge Villanueva.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Just one follow-up question on that. Did you give the witness a copy of the forensic report?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: No, your honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: No, because I was wondering, Mr. Presiding Officer, a while ago, if I heard it right from the witness, that he himself did not even get a chance to actually read the forensic report. So he doesn't have any copy of that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: That's accurate, your honor. That's why... Part of our questioning is to confront actual portions of that report and asking him of his general comments there.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: I'm just wondering because if he is to refute the report, then he should have seen the report, should have read the report. I'm just wondering. Thank you, Mr. President.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: With all due respect, Your Honor, we just wanted to do it in open court. We didn't want to have any prior correspondence with the subpoenaed witness.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Because that's the thing that I'm going to do later on when we get the chance to ask questions. We will be asking him about the forensic report because we feel that he is the best person to refute the forensic report. Now, if he cannot answer these questions, then... For me, it's going to be useless.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We are okay with that, Your Honor, with that methodology. It's really up to, we submit to the court's wisdom on how they want to confront this witness later.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Okay, thank you. Thank you for that clarification. How the senator judges will ask or make interjections and how the senator judges in the court will appreciate the testimony of this witness. Yes, what is the pleasure of Senator Judge Raffy Tulfo?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Dudugtuhan ko lang ang sinabi kanina ni Senator Villanueva. Kung i-refute niya ang forensic expert witness and yet hindi pala siya nabigyan ng kopya ng mga dokumento present ng expert witness. So hindi dapat siya pwedeng mag-refute o kumontra dahil in the first place wala siyang idea kung ano yung mga nakasaad doon sa sinabi ng testigo yung forensic expert witness. At pinasenta rito, maliban na lamang sa on the spot, pinagtatanong ng defense. So dapat, beforehand, he was given a copy of those documents para makapag-aralan niya, para makapagawa siya ng research, para in that case, magiging intelligent, he will be well informed, and he can give intelligent assessment doon sa pag-refute. Sa mga sinabi nung forensic witness, sa ngayon kasi wala eh. Wala siyang kaalam-alam, Mr. Presiding Officer. Wala talaga. Zero. Nagtakangaw kanina, pati ba naman yung, ano ba to? G-Wagon, mag-witness sa G-Wagon, ano ba to? Salesman na rin. I mean, baka mamaya eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The court reminds the gallery to kindly not react or avoid reacting to statements made by anyone in this chamber.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: I mean, sorry, parang gina - Maybe it's not your fault. I'm not gonna fault you on this. Maybe ang problema sa defense, sobrang bilib sila sa iyo, pero hindi mo siguro kayang panindigan yung kasobrang kabiliban nila sa iyo na kung ano na lang pinapasok at sinusubo sa iyo na hindi mo kayang panindigan, hindi mo kayang sasagot. Nagmumakatuloy ikaw na parang alam mo na, hindi mo kagagawa niyong kundi kagagawa ng defense. Maraming salamat po, Mr. President Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Duly noted, Senator Judge Raffy, what is the pleasure of Senator Judge Bam?

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: On this note, Mr. President Officer, Mr. Witness,

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Any documents provided to you before appearing here?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: None, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: So, none of the AMLA records that we subpoenaed were shown to you? Yung mga bank statements, insurance, placements, GIS ng mga kumpanya, were any of these shown to you?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: None, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: None? Okay, so I take it the defense is asking you about the report in terms of concepts.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And on the basis, Your Honor, of actual portions. Because it's a 50-page report, Your Honor, so we just wanted to focus on several portions of that report by confronting him in open court of those portions and then asking him about concepts.

turns.speaker: Sen. Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino
turns.text: Okay, so it's really concepts and general ideas about... Amla, and Financial Investigations. Okay? Kasi, Mr. Witness, and again, di mo naman itong kasalanan, but many times, we have witnesses here, pag tinatanong na namin, ang sagot sa amin, di ho namin alam. So, gusto namin ng mga witness na pwede kaming saguting diretso talaga. Because we just want to find out, we just want to find out the truth, we want to know your opinion. but on specific matters also. So, anyway, you're here and later on may cross, later on magtatanong kami, pero ang ayaw naming marinig is yung sunod-sunod na hindi ko po alam, hindi ko po nabasa, hindi ko po, di ba? Kasi ang nangyayari parang wala rin tayong narating na totoong opinion o totoong pananaw dito sa mga bagay-bagay. Thank you, thank you, Mr. President.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: What is the pleasure of Senator Judge Erwin, the remarks of the Hon. Aquino are generally noted.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Mr. Presiding Officer, quick manifestation lamang po. Kung wala pong nakakita ng mga dokumento itong testigo po na ito, lahat po na sinasabi niya kanina pa, kanina pang umaga, may aabutin na tayo ng alas 6 ng gabi, lahat po ito ay theoretical and cannot be rebutted, documented as documented financial intelligence, Mr. Presiding Officer. Kahit na nanggaling pa siya dyan sa AMLC, etc. na yung kanyang expertise. Kung hindi naman niya po nakita pala ay mga dokumento, STRs, CTRs. What good is it? Para anong titistigo niya? E puro ito theory sa kanyang paningin, sa kanyang paniniwala. I think the defense. I know that you can do better than that. Siguro this coming days, get a witness. Now, who can really stand up? I'm just telling you now to prepare. Get somebody who can really stand up, who can really answer questions from the senator judges. Because mamaya ito, papawisan ito, baka hindi na makasagot ito. I mean, medyo mahina po, I'm sorry ha, mahina po yung the witnesses that you're presenting here these past few days. I cannot dictate that, but I'm just saying, that's my opinion there. Against somebody who can really ika nga na professional, na who can rebut yung mga sanasabi ng prosecution, makakasagot po. Maraming salamat po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We respect the opinion. We know the manifestations of the Senator.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, what is the pleasure of Senator Judge Risa Hontiveros?

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: If I may, Mr. Presiding Officer, just a quick follow-up question to the questions raised right now by the colleague Senator Judges. If I may.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Salamat po, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Atty. Dela Fuente, kasasabi niyo na lamang po ngayon na hindi niyo po nabasa ang forensic report na earlier inihain sa korteng ito ni Atty. Cabrera. Tama po?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Pero at least nabasa niyo po ba o nasimulan man lang iscan, natignan niyo po ba yung mga iba't ibang records na sinupinas, sinumite sa korteng ito na pinagbasehan? Atty. Cabrera sa kanyang inihaing forensics report sa amin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor, hindi po kasi ito ay confidential. Wala akong authority to look into those documents.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
