turns.text: So, ibig sabihin, with all due respect po, sa ngayon, wala po kayo sa solid na posisyon na suriin. Yung kalidad or katotohanan or solidong basehan kahit po sa general principles nung forensic report na iyon ni Atty. Cabrera.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Meron po, Your Honor. As flashed on the screen, I echo what the law says. So base lang po sa batas, maaari ko na akong sagutin kung ano yung nasa... Na ito ba ay lawful or hindi? Yun po ang ginagawa ko ngayon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Alright. So lastly, follow up sa ngayon, Atty. De La Fuente. Kasunod ng mga prinsipyo ngayon na kung bibigyan niyo po ng benefit of the doubt si Atty. Cabrera noon na nagsisikap siyang sumunod din sa mga batayang prinsipyo ng inyong propesyon, dahil kayo po ay peer, kayo po ay colleague kay Atty. Cabrera, Masasabi niyo po ba na may misrepresentation kay Atty. Cabrera na tawagin siyang supposed expert sa field ninyo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, I have a high respect for, respect for Atty. Cabrera. His professional and personal opinions po ay nirerespeto natin siya. But pagdating sa batas, again, we have to abide kung ano yung tama ba, nasa tamang proseso po ba, ang kanyang methodologies po ba ay tama. So ang ginagawa ko lang po, binabangga ang kanyang ginawa doon sa kung ano ang meron sa batas. Kung ito po ba ay mag-a-align. Yun ang aking role dito. Kaya nga sabi ko, I don't need to, ito sa sarili ko, to read the full report even before going here. Because kahit i-flash yan ngayon pa lang, makikita niyo na po, aligned po ba ito sa mga provisions ng AMLA? or hindi.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Sa huli po, at least, salamat naman sa pinahayag niyong pagrespeto bilang peer ninyo kay Atty. Cabrera and I'm willing to guess kung itinanong namin sa kanya noon, sasabihin din niya sa kahit sinong colleague. So at the very least po, and in closing dito sa interjection ko, dahil tinanggap po ng Korte na isa sa mga expert witnesses sa trial na ito si Atty. Cabrera, at the very least, nire-respeto niyo po ba? Yung ganyang pagtanggap ng Korte kay Atty. Cabrera bilang isa sa mga expert witnesses sa trial na ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Risa Hontiveros
turns.text: Maraming salamat po, Atty. De La Fuente. Salamat, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Imee, what is your pleasure, ma'am?

turns.speaker: Sen. Imee Marcos
turns.text: Yes, maraming salamat sa ating presiding judge. At nakikinig po ako sa aking mga kasamahan dito sa Senado. Subalit, ipapaalala ko lang sa lahat na si Lady Justice o yung babaeng justisya ay bulag na katakipang mata. Kasi hindi kinakailangan na basahin ang bawat dokumento, alamin ang mga personalidad, dahil pantay-pantay ang timbang sa batas. Yun lang po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Camille? What is your pleasure, ma'am?

turns.speaker: Sen. Camille Villar
turns.text: Yes, hello, good afternoon po. Just a quick manifestation. I think we've been listening to this witness and I have to say that while he probably hasn't seen the documents that were given by the AMLC, I distinctly remember even the supposed expert witness ng prosecution, si Atty. Cabrera, meron po siyang mga figures dun sa kanyang report of the alleged unexplained wealth that was based on, and it was in the forensic report, that was based on research on the internet. There were also certain facts that he put that also he had very little or no basis for saying. And I think we respected that and accepted that.

turns.speaker: Sen. Camille Villar
turns.text: Personally, I would like to hear the thoughts and opinions of our witness, especially regarding theories because I think while some of his answers to the questions that are being asked by both the defense and the prosecution is of his expert opinion, I think they are of universal principles. Some accounting principles are also universal. So he can answer that even without seeing the specific documents. And I think we listened to the expert witness, to the forensic witness, the financial forensic witness of the prosecution. I think we should also give due time to the expert witness of the defense.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Chair notes. Kala ko pupunta ka sa kantin eh.

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Yes. Just one quick manifestation, Mr. Presiding Officer. Number one, let me again put on record that we have been listening attentively to the respondent's line of questioning despite the fact that it's beyond the issuance of the subpoena and the boundaries set forth by the court inasmuch as the process is concerned. We have no problems with that, Mr. President. In fact, I wanted to palawigin nga, Mr. President, Mr. Presiding Officer, yung ginagawa ng depensa kung siya ay isang forensic expert, kung siya ay magre-refute noong forensic report. I'm more than willing to listen. In fact, kayo na po nagsabi, Mr. President, at inamin na po ng defense lawyer na nagbibigay tayo ng leeway sa kanila. And we have been, we should be continuously giving leeway to be able to understand clearly. But ang hindi po kasi maganda kung unlimited yung magiging

turns.speaker: Sen. Joel Villanueva
turns.text: Scope ng pagiging testigo ng isang witness. And again, we respect the witness. We feel that he is indeed an expert sa issue ng money laundering activities. And again, Mr. Presiding Officer, we're willing to listen to him as long as nandun pa rin sa tamang jurisdiction. At yun nga pong aking masidhing pagnanais ay Matanong po siya mamaya dun sa forensic report para nang sa ganoon makita po natin yung kabilang side, yung kabilang face. Noong pong nangyaring pag-testigo, noong pong forensic expert ng prosecution. Now, if he is not the forensic expert ng defense, I am more than willing to listen in the coming days kung meron pong forensic expert ang defense to refute yung mga binanggit naman ni Atty. Cabrera. Maraming salamat, Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Senator Judge Raffy. Kindly turn on the mic of Senator Judge Raffy.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kasi... Kanina pa tayo dito at parang nagiging super witness na siya, ika nga sabi kanina. Now, very simple question lang dito kay Mr. Witness. Kanina, if you remember, I asked you kung ikaw ba ay nakapagkompleto na ng isang kaso while you were in AMLC. You said yes?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: You sure? You're under oath?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, and ano yung kaso ngayon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Hindi ko po siya dahil... As part of the confidentiality, hindi ko po masabi.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: What if I would present to you an evidence later on na wala kang naikompletong kaso at wala ka pang naifile na kaso whatsoever while you were in AMLC? What if I can present that evidence?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Personally, Your Honor, it's the agency who files, hindi ko ako yung personal.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Kasi sabi mo kanina nung tinanong kita, kanina-kanina pa, na ikaw pa yung nakapag-investigate, nakapagbuo na ng isang kaso. What if I can show you proof later on na wala talaga, so pwede ka makontempt?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As far as I can remember, Your Honor, I signed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: You signed?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy T. Tulfo
turns.text: Pwede ma-refute yan later on. So doon pa nga lang, Mr. Presiding Officer, nagkaka-problema na eh. Sinasabi niya na meron na siyang nabuo na kaso hanggang sa na-efile, when in fact, ang pagkakaalam ko, wala. Wala pa talaga. And he's just claiming it, and like I said, later on, pwede akong kukuha ng ebidensya na wala pa siyang nabuo ng kaso at baka makontemplan ito. Thank you, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We note, The manifestations made by all of the senator judges. However, the court cannot dictate nor impinge upon how either party will present their evidence in chief, much less dictate their strategy in choosing their respective witnesses. I urge our colleagues to...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Exercise more leeway and patience with the presentation being made by the counsel for the respondent. Senator Imee is correct. Habang sinisimbolo ng babaeng sumisimbolo sa ustisya na nakatakip ang mata niya, hindi po nakatakip yung kanyang mga tenga. Ibig sabihin, huwag tayong magbasa base sa panlabas na kanyuan. Makinig at pakinggan din natin kung anong sinasabi, hindi lamang ng mga testigo, pero ganyan din, ng magkabilang panig. I ask for the indulgence of our colleagues and ask Attorney Mark II to take note of the manifestations made and be sensitive to them to a certain extent in continuing with this direct examination with this witness. You may proceed, Attorney Mark.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Okay, so I'll just abbreviate some of the portions, Your Honor. In respect of what the Senator Judges have manifested. So, we're talking about financial investigation about public officials as well. My question is, in an impeachment process, how does the Bill of Rights apply insofar as that impeachable officials' rights when financial investigations are being conducted against that person?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: During the course of the financial investigation, Your Honor, Bill of Rights, the rights of the accused are still intact. In fact, meron ho siyang mga legal remedies along the way.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And how does due process, which is part of the Bill of Rights, apply in financial investigations of an impeachable official, if at all?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, it is still intact. Meron ho legal remedies, right of the accused to answer, opportunity to present evidence in his or her defense.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, I'll just abbreviate other portions of the Bill of Rights, but let me direct your attention to Article 14, Section 3 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights to which the Philippines is a signatory. And I'll just end with this point, Your Honor, for this portion. In the determination of any criminal charge against him, everyone shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality. A. To be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him. My question is in line with that provision that we just read. What is the value of informing the person that you're investigating promptly and completely of the charges against him?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, this is financial investigation, Your Honor. Again, the right of the accused. To confront the evidences presented and also answer with the proper court. Yun po ay importante pa rin.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, thank you. Sige, move on na po tayo. Dito po sa impeachment na to, Atty. De La Fuente, yung conviction or acquittal ni VP Sara, she was voted in 2022 by 32,208,417 na Pilipino. Nakasalalay po ito sa boto ng ating mga mahal na senador ngayon, 24 of them. And ang pagboto and conviction ay nakabase na lamang sa isang article of impeachment. Yun po yung unexplained wealth, alleged unexplained wealth. These constitute the formal charges against the impeachable officer. Just to eliminate doubt, balikan lang po natin yung article na yun. Again, yung tatlo kasing article na withdraw na. Kapag binalikan natin itong Article 2, attorney de la Fuente, says here, Respondent Vice President Sara Z. Duterte committed culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayed public trust when she, letter A, amassed unexplained wealth manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income and earnings during her incumbency as a public official. Letter B, failed to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth, or SALN, including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024. And Letter C, failed to divest and instead willfully continued all her business interests during her tenure as Vice President. For the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. So as regards letter A, so we don't mislead the public, we just want to be more precise. This is what the articles of impeachment charge or is part of their charge. And I'll read. From 2007 to 2024, the net worth of respondent and her spouse rose from 7 million to 88 million. or a total increase of around 80 million. However, as shown earlier, the lawful income of respondent and her spouse for the same period only amounts to roughly 30 million. The difference between their lawful income of 30 million and the increase in their net worth of around 80 million, resulting in a disparity of approximately 50 million, clearly constitutes unexplained wealth. So yun po yung charge. Financial investigator po kayo. Base lang po sa bahaging ito po ng charges, may approximation po na 50 million na unexplained wealth daw po. Okay, according to that charge. Ano pong masasabi niyo po sa kalidad na paratang na ito bilang basihan ng pag-convict or pag-acquit kay VP Sara?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Given that the witness has admitted that he has not read the entire report, and that he has not been given access to any of the documents in this case, he would not be competent to render an opinion on that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yeah, but this is not the report. This is the articles

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: of impeachment. If he knows, if you know, Attorney Rainer, kindly respond.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor, for this one, I leave it to the discretion of our Honorable Impeachment Court and I leave it to the wisdom of our Impeachment Court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, I'll move on to a new allegation or part of the allegation.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Let me direct your attention to pages 13 to 14 of the articles of impeachment. Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV disclosed that a significant portion of this wealth was sourced from illegal activities, including funds linked to illegal drug operations and associations with drug syndicates, and identified specific transactions and individuals connected to the drug trade. These disclosures are corroborated by the findings of the AMLC, which flag billions of pesos in transactions involving respondent and her spouse, reflecting patterns consistent with money laundering and predicate offenses. Notably, a certain name identified in the AMLC records corresponds with those publicly disclosed by Trillanes. Taken together, these facts establish a pattern of criminal enrichment and demonstrate that respondent's wealth is manifestly unlawful, grossly disproportionate to legitimate income, and constitutes ill-gotten wealth. Clear grounds for impeachment. Alright, I'll just go straight to the point, Atty. De La Fuente. Those are the charges, but number one, former Senator Trillanes was not presented. No illegal activity was ever identified. No drug operations with drug syndicates were discussed. No discussion about money laundering and the amount laundered. And no discussion also about any predicate crime. And yet the paragraph ends with, and I quote, Taken together, these facts establish a pattern of criminal enrichment and demonstrates that respondent's wealth is manifestly unlawful, grossly disproportionate to illegal. Legitimate income and constitutes ill-gotten wealth. Clear grounds for impeachment. My only question is this. As a seasoned financial investigator, how clear or viable are these charges of unexplained wealth against the Vice President?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As to viability, as to the viability of the charges, again, Your Honor, I leave it to the Court to decide if these charges would warrant

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Decision on conviction or acquittal. So, it's really up to the court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Punta naman po tayo dun sa letter B or yung nondisclosure in the SALN. Last couple of pages, Your Honor, if I may be allowed to just finish. Contrary to her declarations in the SALN, Respondent and her spouse owned and acquired billions of pesos which were deposited from 2007 to 2024 in their bank accounts. These funds deposited in their bank accounts were not declared in Respondent's SALNs, including in her SALNs covering the years 2022, 2023, and 2024. Despite the billions of pesos deposited in respondent and her spouse's bank accounts from 2007 to 2024, these deposits were not declared as cash on hand, cash in bank, or other personal assets in respondent's SALNs, including in her SALNs for 2020 to 2023 and 2024. Again, ganun lang po yung allegation na nakalagay sa articles of impeachment. And I quote, owned and acquired billions of pesos. which were deposited from 2007 to 2024 in their bank accounts. And then these funds deposited in their bank accounts were not declared in respondent SALNs, including in their SALNs covering the years 2020 to 2024. Again, my only question as a financial investigation, ano ang effect? Maybe you can answer not in lieu of the facts of this case, but what is the effect if the accusation of financial wrongdoing is vague?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, Your Honor, the last

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: part. What is the effect of a vague accusation of financial wrongdoing as a financial investigator?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. There's nothing vague about the quoted portion that is a conclusion on the part of the...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly reform your question, Attorney Mark. Just ask him directly what his opinion is of the allegation you read in the articles. If you can.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Opinion on this, Your Honor. Again, the question... If there's ambiguity or vagueness, well, that would weaken. But again, I defer to the wisdom of the Honorable Impeachment Court how they appreciate these observations.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We respect that. Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Your Honor, I'm very sorry to interrupt. Before we continue, could we have a very brief CR break? It's a one or two minute break. I think the witness also may need to...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Do you need to go, Atty. Rainer?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Chair declares a three-minute bathroom break.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. I'm winding up, Your Honor. We decided to obviate certain portions.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly proceed, Atty. Morris.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Alright, let me direct your attention to Article 3, Section 3 of the 1987 Constitution. It says here, The privacy of communication and correspondence shall be inviolable except upon lawful order of the court or when public safety or order requires otherwise as prescribed by law. Any evidence obtained in violation of this or the preceding section shall be inadmissible for any purpose in any proceeding. In line with this provision and your experience also as a financial investigator, kindly explain the concept of fishing expedition. If you know. or if you can recall.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Well, on fishing expedition, Your Honor, this is again initiated under that constitutional provision. It protects the individual from any arbitrary state intrusion, ensuring that privacy of communication and also information relating to the individual is being safeguarded. So pinaprotectahan po ng ating Constitution. Ang panghihimasok, walang habas na panghihimasok sa informasyon na ito provided na kung ito man ay in relation sa ongoing investigation o sa isang kaso, dapat sundin pa rin ang mga safeguards provided ng batas. Hindi ho ito unlimited authority to disclose and... Discloses information.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, and what is the effect of fishing expedition in terms of documents used as evidence in an impeachment trial, if at all?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So ito ay considered na fruits of a poisonous tree. These are inadmissible as evidence.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright, thank you po. I'm about to conclude. Yung term na ill-gotten wealth actually appears once in the Constitution. Let me direct your attention to Article 18, Section 26.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Let me read. The authority to issue sequestration or freeze orders under Proclamation No. 3 dated March 25, 1986 in relation to the recovery of ill-gotten wealth shall remain operative for not more than 18 months after the ratification of this Constitution. However, in the national interest as certified by the President, the Congress may extend such period. My only question about this article is this. If you know, based on the history of our 1987 Constitution, kaninong ilgaten wealth po ba yung tinutukoy ng probisyong ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: For this specific provision, there's no specific individual, official, or entity mentioned po dito sa Section 26 in Article... At any rate,

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: how important po ba is it to look back on the history of our Constitution as we undertake the impeachment process today? If you can just give your opinion on that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Napaka-importante ho. Our history would dictate our future. So we have to look back kung ano man ang sarkomstansyang nakapaligid nung naisulat ho ang batas na ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Last set of figures before I end. Let me show you VP Sara's recent ratings in the 2028 Presidential Preference Surveys. So I'll just show you three surveys.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So Sara Duterte leads 2028 Presidential Preference in Pulse Asia. So there's the rating. And then next survey, Sara Duterte maintains commanding lead in 2028 Presidential Preferences. And then there's the one with, I think this is OCTA, Current Presidential Voting Preference. And I'm about to end. We all know that impeachment carries the penalty of disqualification to hold any office under the Republic of the Philippines. This is my second to the last question and it is quite a personal one. Since iisa na lang naman po yung charge against VP Sara. Again, you can answer based on the factual milieu of what you know from this case or based on your opinion. What is the seriousness po? What is the seriousness of financial wrongdoing that warrants a conviction in an impeachment case? Your Honor, again, let me repeat the question, considering also, granting that these surveys, that VP Sara, the, well, the choice of the people based on these surveys, what is the seriousness of financial wrongdoing that warrants VP Sara's conviction?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Seriousness of financial wrongdoing that warrants...

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Conviction in this impeachment case. Gusto niyo po bang tagalogin para mas may time kayo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sige nga po.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Gano po ba kagrabe or ano po ba yung bigat ng financial wrongdoing that will warrant yung conviction ng isang tao sa isang impeachment proceeding?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Dapat ito ay may absolute certainty po tayo. Given we are impeaching a high-ranking official, the findings should be based on facts, not conjectures. At dapat ito, yung magiging desisyon ng ating impeachment court must

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: uphold the rule of law.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So ang ating magiging desisyon, it should... Encapsulate yung prinsipyo na our law should protect the innocent as aggressively as it pursues the guilty.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you. One last question, Your Honor. And I'll end with a preamble. The preamble states we, the sovereign Filipino people, imploring the aid of Almighty God. And then the lawyers would know the rest of the preamble. But my question is this, and it's again quite a personal question. You are a lecturer. You mentioned that you have students and you have an influence on the next generation. How important is it to implore the aid of Almighty God in such a time as this when the ongoing impeachment has greatly divided our beloved country?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, very important, Your Honor. There are things that are beyond our explanation, beyond our comprehension. So it's really important that all of our decisions should be guided. by the Divine. And again, we have to be aware that whatever our decision will be, will have long-lasting effects sa ating bansa.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Thank you. Your Honor, just no more questions, just a manifestation, Your Honor. Again, we respect the sentiments, Your Honor, of our senator judges. But again, and this is coming from a personal standpoint, and I know I'm not authorized to speak on behalf of this witness, Your Honor, but as a colleague in the profession, We have an oath, Your Honor, and we're just doing our job, trying to do our job in the best possible way, Your Honor. We do not want to impede on any rights of other peoples, as well as the rights of the prosecution to make their own case. But, Your Honor, our goal in this whole exercise is really to ferret out the truth and provide two sides of the coin, Your Honor. And we hope, Your Honor, that this will be well taken as well by the Senate Impeachment Court. Thank you, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We note the manifestation of Attorney Mark as stated by the Presiding Officer earlier. Liyue has been given and patience has been extended not only by the Presiding Officer but by members of the Impeachment Court as well. Attorney, Honorable Chel Cross.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: With the permission of the Honorable Court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, sir.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Good afternoon, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You started out in the Anti-Money Laundering Council in July of 2015.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: July of 2015, Your Honor. Correct.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And you were part of the Compliance and Investigation Group only until August of 2017. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2018. Yes, Your Honor. But I'm still part of the Secretariat after.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: August 2017. Let's be clear about that. You were only a financial investigator for a period of 24 months. July 2015 up to August 2017. 25 months. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Roughly, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes. You were only a financial investigator for 25 months at the AMLA. You started in July of 2015. and ended as a financial investigator in August of 2017. Isn't that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: In fact, in August of 2017, you were taken out of the compliance and investigation group and reassigned to the technical services staff under the office of the Executive Director. No longer doing any form of investigation. Isn't that true?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The first part of the statement is...

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: My answer, my question is very simple. Sir, you're a lawyer, you're a CPA. You can answer it by yes or no. Your defense counsel can ask you to explain later if they want to.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The question again, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You were only a... After you were assigned from the... or taken out of the compliance and investigation group and transferred to the TSS... or Technical Services Staff under the Office of the Executive Director. Your work was really more on information campaign awareness, right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, before the witness answers, can we just ask for leeway so that the witness will be allowed to answer freely without interruption?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: He's on cross, counsel. You can address whatever issues he needs to clarify on redirect. Witness, will please answer the question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The answer is

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: yes,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: but can I explain, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Later, if your lawyer wants to ask you to explain.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Can he be allowed at this time, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Counsel, the Honorable Diokno already got his answer. Again, without prejudice to you asking him to explain and redirect, we will not prohibit him.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: The Technical Services Staff under the Office of the Executive Director is a totally different office from the Compliance and Investigation Group, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, your honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: In fact, the technical services staff serves as staff to the office of the executive director. It has no investigative functions at all.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, your honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: In other words, your only background or expertise, quote-unquote, claimed expertise as a financial investigator is the 25 months you served as an FI under the compliance and investigation group. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: May I explain, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You may answer my question. Perhaps later you may explain if your lawyer wants to ask you.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, you started out, what was your position, Sir? BSP ranking?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Bank Officer 2.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And Bank Officer 2. So that is not a senior management position, am I correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Yes. That's entry level.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Entry level. And you were never promoted from bank officer too?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: No, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So your expertise or your claimed expertise as a financial expert in financial investigation only comes from the 25 months you were an entry-level investigator for the AMLC. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You would agree with me that a financial investigation under the AMLA involves investigation of money laundering and its predicate crimes. Tama po ba iyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Money laundering, Your Honor, not the predicate crime.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Ah, money laundering. Thank you. I stand corrected. So iba po ang trabaho ng isang financial investigator kung ang iniinvestigahan niya ay unexplained wealth, non-declaration ng SALN, At participation in business. Wala pong kinalaman ang financial investigator ng AMLA doon sa mga bagay na iyon, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes po. Yun po kasi ay predicate crime, iba pong ahensya.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Tama po iyon. Now, as a member of the TSS, yung pong technical services staff under the office of the executive director, Ang naging trabaho niyo ay capacity building at information awareness campaign. Di po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Isa po sa mga trabaho.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So your employers felt that you would be more appropriate to serve AMLA no longer as a financial investigator. I'm not yet finished, Your Honor, please. But rather, you would best... Provide services to AMLA as a member of the TSS.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. The witness will not be competent to answer that question. It's also argumentative.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: If he knows, counsel. It's not argumentative, but if he knows.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Iniwan ko po yan sa discretion ng aming leadership during that time. So ako ko kasi kung ano man ang iba tong trabaho, kagawin ko natin yan.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Alright. Noong dalawang taon na kayo ay isang AMLA financial investigator, how long... On the average, would it take for you to complete one investigation?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Depende ho kung simple or complex cases. Depende ho ito.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Let's talk about complex cases. Sorry to interrupt you. Mga more or less, gaano katagal po yung isang investigation na gano'n?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Para ho makapag-come up ng isang financial investigation report, normally, three weeks to one month, or even, but it won't go beyond two months.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So, in other words, your only experience actual on the ground during those 25 months was the assigned cases given to you, which according to you, complex, could take several months. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: For complex, but it's mixed with other cases, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So let's say from July 2015 up to August of 2017, if every complex investigation took several months, you would not have been able to complete more than 20 or 30 of those. Would that be a fair statement?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: If the witness knows, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I would have to overrule, counsel. Witness may answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The question again, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Sabi po ninyo kanina na yung mga komplikadong mga investigasyon ay umaabot minsan ng ilang buwan. Considering po na kayo ay dalawang taon lamang naging financial investigator ng AMLA, yung mga natapos nyong complex na financial investigation, hindi po maaaring lumampas ng mga dalawampu o tatlumpung kaso.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Maaaring lumampas kasi during that time, Lean Manpower ang AMLC. So we are really multitasking. Kaya humabalik ako doon sa kanina inyong nabanggit. Ako ay nasa TSS. But the cases that I was initially assigned, I still continue handling them.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: At yun lang po ang masasabi niyong experience ninyo sa pag-iinvestiga ng mga pinansyal na bagay na nasa AMLC kayo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: As an answer, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Move on, counsel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Ngayon, You only became an accredited AMLA trainer, you said earlier, after you left already the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2019, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: In fact, you are testifying here today based on your short stint as a financial investigator and also on your knowledge of general principles of anti-money laundering. Is that not correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Wala po kayong... Nakita o nabasa ng kabuuan na forensic report ni Atty. Cabrera. You did not read the entire report.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Hindi po, Your Honor. Sa mga news lang po.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You did not look at any of the bank records that Atty. Cabrera examined.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Hindi po dahil confidential po ito.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You did not have a look at any of the records produced by the Bureau of Internal Revenue to this Court. Hindi niyo rin po naalam yun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Same answer, Your Honor. Confidential po kasi ito.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Hindi niyo rin po nakita yung records ng SEC o Securities and Exchange Commission na binigay po nila dito sa hukumang ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ah, hindi po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Pati po yung mga records na binigay ng insurance companies, lahat po ng ebidensya na nandito sa loob nitong hukumang ito, wala kayong binasa.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Hindi po dahil hindi po ako yung intended end user.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So, any opinions that you may give have no basis in any factual evidence provided in this court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. That's misleading. It already calls for a conclusion of law that only this honorable court has the function to do.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Kindly reform. I know where you're getting at, Honorable Chel. Kindly reform.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You have stated, you have made a variety of opinions about The report of Atty. Cabrera about methodologies that were employed. But you have no personal knowledge of what exactly was done by Atty. Cabrera in preparing his report. Is that right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So ano ngayon ang bigat ng inyong opinion kung wala naman pala kayong alam tungkol sa mga ginawa ni Atty. Cabrera?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Question is argumentative, Your Honor. And already, again, calls for a conclusion of fact and law.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: He said ano-anong ayan ang halbigat or halaga.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: No, I heard a question. If you know, Attorney Rainer, if you wish to answer and if you know.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Ang akin lang hung saligan ay ang ating amla, ang ating batas. So I can answer based on the law. I echo, I mirror what the law says. So hindi ko daw kailangan... Ako personally ayokong basahin yung report because coming here... and awala rin akong akses sa report. Coming here, reading that report, I will develop biases. I will be swayed doong report na iyon. So ang akin lang kung sinasandalan dito ay kung ano ang nasa batas.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, your knowledge of AMLA operations is limited, your personal knowledge of AMLA operations is limited to your brief stint as a financial investigator of AMLA. Isn't that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Brief but meaningful. Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And as far as any current policies, practices, procedures of the AMLA, wala po kayong personal knowledge doon mula nung kayo'y umalis noong 2018.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Internal policies, none. But those that would affect covered persons, yes.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yung kaalaman ninyo about the anti-money laundering concepts ay...

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Na-acquire ninyo after you left. Well, let me reform. What you know about the anti-money laundering concepts is the same as what any other lawyer who reads the law would know. Isn't that right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, I respect po. Na-develop po ito nung ako'y nasa loob pa at nung ako'y lumabas na. Mas lalo na-develop because aside from getting the insights sa public sector, nakita ko rin ho, I was able to harmonize, marry kung ano ba yung meron sa private sector.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Nabasa ko po yung inyong curriculum vitae. Tama po ba na wala naman ako nakita doon na meron kayong special knowledge, experience, training, or education in investigating cases of unexplained wealth. Tama po ba yan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Meron po, Your Honor. I think this was trainings conducted by USAID, anti-corruption, and then meron din po sa international. ILEA, International Law Enforcement Academy in Thailand. So meron siyang financial investigation po, session 7. So I was able to, I was sent by the office to go there and participate, represent the office po namin.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: But as you mentioned earlier, your work is for the AMLA, involved financial investigation of money laundering. Tama po?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes. Now, I noticed as well from your background that you, while you did serve in other agencies... Let me go through this one by one. Yung una niyong trabaho ay sa BIR, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct po.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Earlier on direct, you said you served there at least one year. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Working student po ako doon.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: But it would appear that you were only working there for 11 months.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Short of one year.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Short of one year. Short of

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: one month.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: One year short of one month with the BIR. Your second job was with Punong Bayan and Aralio. How many months did you work at Punong Bayan and Aralio?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Just for two months, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Two months. And your third job was with the GCG, Governance Commission for GLCCs. How many months did you serve in that office?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Two years, Your Honor. Before, I think, almost a few months after two years.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: My records indicate that you started in April 2012 and ended in January 2014. Would that be accurate?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Around that time, yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So that's not two years. That's 21 months.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Roughly, yeah.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And your next job was at the Commission on Elections where you served there for 17 months.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: January 2014 to June 2015.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And that is the summa total of your qualifications as a financial expert that you are peddling before this court?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: No, Your Honor. That is the history of my government and private employment. Insofar as financial investigation, that would start with AMLC up to until now that I'm into private practice. It continues up to the present.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, you said you worked for Punong Bayan and Aralio for two months. So this did not give you any opportunity to learn how to conduct forensic audits, how to conduct compliance and due diligence, and other auditing services that are usually offered by these kinds of firms. Isn't that right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I was assigned at the tax division. I am a senior tax associate. So the engagements that we handle are tax assessments. and also due diligence review. Yeah, we did that.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So wala po kayong ginawa o sinagawang forensic audits?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Wala po. Iba pong grupo ang audit.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Alright. Now, let me move on to, well, first of all, insofar as your work as a financial investigator, ever since you left the Anti-Money Laundering Council, Wala na po kayong contact sa mga nasa opisina ng AMLA?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Wala po. After leaving the service 2018, I started my own, well, with a friend po, we started a law office. So I imposed a one year, wala po talaga, that's for one year, no AML related work. That's a, kumbaga, delikadesa na rin po namin.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you. You were asked about Section 8-A of Republic Act 9160. May I know, how many times was the Anti-Money Laundering Law amended?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Seven times.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, when was the Section 8A put in to the Anti-Money Laundering Law?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: That's 2021 by virtue of Republic Act 11521.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So wala na po kayo sa AMLA noon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And am I correct in reading that law, that particular section? That there is an exception for the orders of the Court of Competent Jurisdiction.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. That's on paragraph 2.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And since the Impeachment Court is a creation of this Constitution, the Impeachment Court is a Court of Competent Jurisdiction. Is that not right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, once that exception applies and now information is subpoenaed by the Impeachment Court, From the Anti-Money Laundering Council. At binigay na po ng Anti-Money Laundering Council yan sa court. That is now within the custody of the court. Is that not right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The last part?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Once that information is submitted to the court, that information is now in the custody of the court.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And it is the court that then will decide on whether what conditions that can be imposed in terms of using that

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor, subject to the same paragraph of Section 8-A.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes, and in fact it's not only the impeachment court that issues subpoenas to the AMLA, even the Sandiganbayan does, am I correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And once the AMLA submits the information to the Sandiganbayan, that can now be included in the decision of the Sandiganbayan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Even up to the Supreme Court, that can be mentioned, right? So, wala na pong espasyo sa confidentiality yan. Basta compelled by court order ang information. Di po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor. Nakalagay ko kasi doon. Merong mga procedures that must be implemented for the protection, handling, and storage of access over such information.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I'm sorry, please continue.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yung confidentiality na yan, hindi nahuhubad kapag yan ay napunta na sa Korte. It travels with the information.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I have to... I wonder about that because I've read and I'm... Have you ever read any Supreme Court decisions that came from an appeal from the Sandigan Bayan that discuss what was presented by AMLA?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sorry, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Is it not a fact that once the AMLA reports are submitted to the Sandigan Bayan, as you said, they can be incorporated in the decision and therefore accessible to the public?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, the witness won't be competent to answer without the good counsel confronting him with the documents.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: If he knows of a case, he was presented as an AMLC expert.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, Your Honor. Can the decision cite portions of the report?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Is that a question? You are familiar with the cases of Ligot, among others. And you will confirm that in the decision of the Supreme Court, Mention there was made of what was presented by the Anti-Money Laundering Council, if not in the legal case, in similar cases of unexplained wealth. Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So in that respect, ay hindi na po confidential yung galing sa AMLA kasi mismo ang Supreme Court na naglabas ng mga nilalaman ng AMLA documents.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: If my memory serves me right, Your Honor, these are findings already. Process information. What... is prohibited is the raw data, intelligence report data, which is subject to verification.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So now you're making these finer distinctions that you did not make earlier. Ang sinasabi po ninyo ngayon, yung raw data lang po ang confidential.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Including the investigation report, Your Honor, not just the raw data, which is a derivative.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Pero yung investigation report nga po ay sinasight mismo ng Supreme Court. So paano siya magiging confidential kung ganon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Counsel is already arguing with the witness, Your Honor. Anyway, the witness already gave his answer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Move on to your next point, Attorney Chell.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, earlier on your direct examination, you testified that there's no such thing as sensitivity analysis.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa batas.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Sa batas.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Wala po.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Ngayon, kayo po ay certified public accountant, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Am I correct in saying that that concept of sensitivity analysis is recognized in the field of accountancy?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So, nagagamit po yan ng mga accountants sa kanilang pag-iinvestiga, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: And there's nothing wrong with a forensic expert applying a sensitivity analysis test in his or her examination. Would that be correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, In connection with that sensitivity analysis, meron din kayong kanina nabanggit na piercing the corporate veil can only be done by the court. Did I get you right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. I base it on my limited knowledge of our revised corporation code.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Limited knowledge of the revised corporation code. Ibig niyo bang sabihin na sa pag-analyze ng isang accountant, Odikaya, financial investigator. Hindi niya pwedeng tingnan kung sino ang totoong may-ari ng isang kumpanya?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Misleading and already assumed sa fact that it has not been established.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: It's not misleading, Your Honor. It's based on the testimony of the witness given.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Misleading, Your Honor, because that's not even the concept that is contemplated by the piercing, the veil of corporate fiction, Doctor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Actually, court would like to hear the witness answer. Court has its own questions with respect to his theory in that regard at the proper time. If you know, Attorney Rainer?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: May I ask again?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Can you repeat the question, Honorable Chel?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Let me just rephrase it. Kanina po, sinabi ninyo na ang korte lang ang pwedeng mag-pierce ng corporate veil. Ang tanong ko po, ibig nyo bang sabihin na hindi maaaring i-apply yung doctrine na yan ng isang CPA o forensic investigator?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa kanya hong analysis, maaari.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So, wala naman pong palang pagkakamali ang ginawa ng forensic experts sa impeachment court na ito sa pag-apply ng piercing the corporate veil sa kasong ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. That's already misleading. Considering, Your Honor, that the good counsel already added his own interpretation to what the forensic analyst allegedly did.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: No, Atty. Mark, the witness answered that it is possible, it can be used. Witness may answer. It came from his own answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: The question again, Your Honor, kung tama ba? Yes, Your Honor, tama naman. Maaari niyang gawin yun. At ano po niyong pangalawang tanong?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Wala pong ginawang pagkakamali si Atty. Cabrera nung in-apply po niya yung doctrine of piercing the corporate veil. Sa kanyang analysis sa kasong ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa kanyang professional report. Wala naman po. Walang nagbabawal sa kanya na gamitin iyon.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you. Thank you for that.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Earlier, you said that you have quote-unquote limited knowledge of constitutional law. Kayo na mismo po na nag-amin yan, di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. I was subpoenaed for AML matters.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So your opinions about What is found in the Constitution are really, don't really have much... Paano po kami makakapaniwala sa sinasabi ninyo sa mga nabanggit ninyong constitutional law opinions kung mismo kayo nagsabi na limited po ang inyong kaalaman tungkol sa saligang batas?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. The witness is already incompetent to answer that question considering that he cannot delve on the minds of... His own listeners, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I will withdraw the question, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Atty. Arnabuchel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, earlier as well, you said that you were asked about legitimate income and you answered to the effect that legitimate income would include income derived from one's profession or business activities. Did I hear you right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor. Correct, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: But if a certain official of the Executive Department is expressly prohibited by the Constitution from receiving any emoluments other than what they receive from their salary, ay hindi na rin po legitimate income yung kita mula sa profesyon. Kasi pinagbabawal mismo ng Constitution eh.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: To the impeachment court to decide whether they would consider this as legitimate or illegitimate given the facts surrounding the case.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: But you would agree with me that under Section 13, Article 7 of the Constitution, the Vice President is not allowed to receive any emoluments other than her salary as Vice President. You would agree with that legal statement?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Again, already calls for a conclusion of law. And that's precisely the question that the court needs to resolve in this impeachment case.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I think the Honorable Chel is quoting the constitutional provision itself. Would that be correct?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: But he's asking already for an interpretation of such provision, Your Honor, that favors their position, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: He also did that, Atty. Mark, but the witness simply answered he defers to the court. He may do so again now.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We will submit, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Yes, Atty. Rainer, if you know.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: If it is what is written in the Constitution, yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So, would your answer now change about what is legitimate income, considering that for the Vice President, income from a profession is not allowed while the Vice President is sitting as such?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Again, I leave it to the discretion of the Honorable Court, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, question. Earlier, you were shown snippets of the report of Attorney Cabrera. You have already testified that you didn't read the whole report. Wouldn't you agree that context means a lot in terms of evaluating the veracity of a financial report?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection. Question is vague, Your Honor. Context means a lot. What does that mean?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I think the witness is intelligent enough

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: to be able to understand the question.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Witness may answer if you know.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As much as I want to read. Your Honor, I have no access over this information. I did my research, reading the news, watching some of the audio clips, and that's it.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Let's turn this around. Let's say that I were going to evaluate your investigation report. Kayo po ba ay nakapagsubmit hindi po ba ng investigation report sa Anti-Money Laundering Council?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Pero sa pag-husga ko, sa pag-evaluate ko ng inyong report, hindi ko muna babasahin yung kabuuan. Hahanap lang ako ng ilan ng mga portion doon. Don't you think that would be unfair to you?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. It's a speculative question, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I think the witness is capable of answering that, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Allow me, Counsel. Atty. Rainer, ang pinupunto lamang naman po ni Hon. Diokno, importante ang konteksto. Ibig sabihin, yung kabuuan... Report para maunawaan yung parte nito at yung mga conclusion nito. Sangahin po ba kayo sa statement na yun na mahalaga ang konteksto at medyo may pagkukulang kapag hindi nyo nakita yung kabuhang report sa pagbibigay ng komentaryo kaugnay sa parte o bahagi lamang ng report?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Correct, Your Honor. Pero ang pagbabahagi ho ng aking opinion sa report ay base lamang ibabanggahos kung ano mang provided ng batas. So I am not countering his or her conclusions.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: As to the acceptability or not, again, we respect the professional, personal opinion of the forensic accountant who did that. But it should have been done within the bounds of law. Yun lang ang aking role. I do not question. Nasa sa ating impeachment court na huyon kung kanila bang tatanggapin o hindi.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You cannot

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: cite any specific action done by Atty. Cabrera that violates the law.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Based on the circumstances, again, it's up to the impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Sir, my question is very simple. Meron pa ba kayong maipapakita ng mismong paglabag ng batas doon sa report ni Atty. Cabrera?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Your Honor, again, the witness was not able to peruse the actual report, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: As to the portion shown to you, Atty. Rainer, as to the portion shown to you, you testified, you made observations earlier, you expressed your opinion earlier. The question of Atty. The Honorable Chel is quite clear. On the portion shown to you and methodology used as described by the counsel when he was asking questions, were any laws, did Atty. Cabrera in his methodology and their presentation violate any laws. In your opinion?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: At Section 8 of RA 9160 as amended. On confidentiality. On confidentiality to a private individual.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Ito yung pagbibigay ng prosecution o ng komite sa kanya ng kopya para pag-aralan, suriin, at pagbasihan ng report. That's the violation.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Pero ito ay, again, depende na ho sa aggrieved party. If he or she will... Pursue that case. So again, nandun na po tayo nakadepende. And

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: that is the only legal provision that you can cite? Nothing else?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: That's the only legal provision on confidentiality, Your Honor. Section 8-A, in relation to that, we have the penal provision on Section 14-D.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yes, so those two related provisions.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Now, considering that the impeachment court itself has allowed Presentation of the Anti-Money Laundering Council Records and also allowed the testimony of Attorney Cabrera. Is it your opinion that that provision is still being violated by the Impeachment Court?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. Question is misleading. What the witness answered was that it was a violation of 8A because the AMLC documents or materials were provided by the prosecution. A third party. Now the counsel is implying your honor that the court authorized such disclosure but the court will never admit your honor that it issued any order authorizing the release of those AMLC documents to attorney Cabrera.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Share confirms that and I believe the prosecution admitted that they gave a copy to attorney Cabrera much much earlier based on the documents received by the Committee on Justice, by virtue of a subpoena issued by the Committee on Justice. Move along, counsel.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Earlier, you questioned the report's reliance or, according to you, use of official receipts from Jollibee Corporation. Ayun pong pinakita sa inyong mga resibo. Those are considered as official receipts from the branches involved, right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: So in other words, those documents have evidentiary weight.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Depende ho yan sa ating impeachment court if they will take it.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: In fact, if a corporation issues a receipt and states that it is their corporation that is issuing the receipt, that is in the nature of an admission by the corporation, is it not?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection, Your Honor. It already calls for conclusions of facts and law, and the witness will not be able to testify on those.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Your Honor, the witness is a lawyer and a CPA. I believe if he knows, he can provide an answer. But

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: it was not covered in his testimony.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: I am entitled to question him on this point on cross-law.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We're giving him enough leeway, counsel. Witness may answer if he knows on the receipts.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ano po, Lee, yung specific question, Your Honor?

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Yung pong mga official receipt na ini-issue ng isang kumpanya ay meron pong evidentiary weight yun, di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: It's not the best evidence obtainable, po. There are... Better evidences po sa ating official certified true copies.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Well, thank you for that. That really wasn't my question. My question is very simple. When a company issues an official receipt and states that it was that company that issued the receipt, mapikat po na ebidensya yun, hindi po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Objection. As an answer, Your Honor, the witness already distinguished Your Honor. The evidentiary weight of such document vis-a-vis other official documents.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Move on, counsel. We get the point.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. I just have a few more questions on cross-examination, but if I may be given just a minute or two to confer with my colleagues, there may be other points that I will raise, if I may, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Without calling a recess, you may do so, counsel.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: We will entertain some interjections then.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: From one or two,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Sotto, former Senate President is recognized.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed with the interjection, sir. You have two minutes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Actually, I have one or two questions, only Mr. Presiding Officer. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Mr. Witness, Attorney Dela Fuente, when did you author that AML handbook?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: July of 2025, Your Honor. It was published, but initial works here started in 2024.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: You worked with the AMLC from 2015 to 2018 only, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Where were you in January 2021?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: January pandemic work, Your Honor, or the actual place?

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: What work? What was your work then?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I was a partner at Gialogo de la Fuente and Associates.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: No longer with AMLC.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Yes. We amended the law in January 2021.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ah, yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Vicente C. Sotto III
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Honorable Chel, are you ready? Senator Judge Lacson, what is your pleasure, sir? Okay. Honorable Chel, you're ready?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Not yet? Senator Judge Lacson, what is your pleasure, sir?

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: Thank you, sir. Presiding Officer. I had actually... Interjected on the issue involving the claim of the same defense counsel about weaponizing AMLC, the AMLC, for political persecution and harassment, when then Executive Director Buenaventura was our witness. Since Atty. Vinluan brought it up again, pinapull out ko na po yung TSN para mas accurate.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: I remember, Honorable Lacson.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: And ang tanong ko po sa witness, familiar pa kayo sa history or provenance ng Section 16 ng AMLA? Kung saan ang galing yung Section 16?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Attorney Rainer, kindly respond.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Not that familiar,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: But I'll tell you, no? Historical. Yeah. Ang nag-introduce niyan, Senator Sotto, Sotto Amendment. Actually, yung kasama niya nag-introduce dito, patay na rin pareho. Si late Joker Arroyo, Senator Arroyo, and Senator Ople, as well as Senator Angara. Siya na lang po ang naiwan.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: Well, I can say na, following yung interjection ni Senators Sotto and Ople, pwede natin madeduce natin na yung present provision of Section 16 on prohibitions against political harassment of the money laundering law including the AMLC on the prohibition against political persecution and harassment was really for the protection not only of trade and commerce but also of a candidate sa eleksyon. Diyan po nagsimula yan. So general lang yung paragraph 1, actually yung 2 yung specific, yun nga inintroduce ni Senator Sotto at that time.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” M. Lacson
turns.text: Kaya nasa amin yung trade and commerce kasi yun yung mga contributors eh. Baka maharas. So hindi pwedeng i-interpret na in a general sense like an impeachment trial na i-apply yung political persecution. Kasi po ako noong 2001 hanggang 2000 when I ended my term in 2013, subject po ako ng political persecution. Money laundering din. Sinasabi nung dating administration ay stashed sa mga foreign banks hundreds of millions of US dollars. Yun ang political persecution. Hindi ko ginamit yung prohibition kasi hindi applicable. Kasi nga applicability ng Section 16, papunta lamang doon sa election period para huwag maharas yung kandidato. I would just like to reiterate that kasi laging nabibring up yung political harassment. Asaka persecution dito sa impeachment trial. Hindi po yung intent and purpose of that provision. Yun lamang po, Mr. Presiding Officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Senator Judge Lacson. Honorable Chell, you may proceed with your cross and wind up.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honor. Earlier, Mr. Witness, good afternoon. You testified that you felt that two weeks was medyo mahirap para magpapagsagawa ng isang financial... Investigation. Tama po ba yan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Challenging po yan. Mahira po.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: But that is on the assumption that the person involved only had two weeks. If that person had several months to begin their examination and as records came in, continued to examine the documents, walang pong issue ang two weeks. Tama po ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Thank you. Now, let me just wind up. I just want to summarize several points that you have mentioned.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You're not saying to this Court that the AMLA records, that the records submitted by AMLA are inaccurate or untruthful. Wala namang kayong sinasabing ganun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Wala po iyon.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: You're not saying that the records submitted by the BIR

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: SEC, and other government agencies are tampered or fabricated. Hindi mo rin sinasabi yun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: None, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Hindi niyo rin sinasabi na hindi totoo yung mga bank records na sinabmit ng mga bank o sa hukumang ito.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: None, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Hindi niyo rin sinasabi, aside from yung mga nabanggit niyo, mga snippets ng report ni Atty. Cabrera, Meron pang ibang mga questionable parts ng report niya dahil hindi mo naman nabasa yung kabuuan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Kung ano lang po yung napakita sa akin, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: Hindi niyo rin sinasabi na, in fact, kanina pinupurin niyo yung qualifications ni Atty. Cabrera bilang forensic expert. So you're not questioning his qualifications.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I still respect him as a fellow professional.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
turns.text: No question. Kasi baka po magka hindi kayo maintindihan o hindi malinaw sa publiko. Kayo po ba, sinasabi ba ninyo na pag walang money laundering, wala rin unexplained wealth? Ano po? Pag walang money laundering, walang unexplained wealth?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Baliktad po. Money laundering is a derivative offense. So, it has to depend on a... Wala kong ilo-launder kung walang krimeng nangyari.

turns.speaker: Rep. Jose Manuel “Chel” I. Diokno
