turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Okay. So, no, and therefore, impeachment court, when it commands or it subpoenas or it compels, that is an authorized disclosure.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan
turns.text: Okay, no other questions. Thank you. Thank you for that clarification, Attorney.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you. No other.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Erwin, my mistake that Senator Kiko was the last. What's your pleasure, Senator Judge Erwin?

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Just a clarificatory question, uh,

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: uh, presiding officer, sir. Uh, you know, testigo, kailan po kayo nagumpisa magtrabaho sa gobyerno? At anong ahensya po ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2009, Your Honor, BIR. BIR.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Kailan po kayo mali sa BIR?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2010, Your Honor, October.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: 2010. Ano po sinulod na pinasukan ninyong ahensya?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Uh... Nag-private po muna ako, punong bayan ni Roland, then Governance Commission for GOCCs noong 2012.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Hanggang kailan po kayo doon sa GOCCs?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2014, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: 2014. Afternoon po, saan po kayo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa Commission on Elections po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Commission on Elections. Anong year naman po kayo doon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2014, before I entered AMLC po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Hanggang kailan po kayo doon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: June, around June or May, Your Honor, 2015.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: After who noon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Sa AMLC Secretariat na po, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Hanggang kailan po kayo doon?

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Alright. After that, sir, tama po ba consultancy na lang po kayo sa...

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Nag-low office pa po, Your Honor. This is a private general professional partnership.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: And then 2021,

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: sarili ko na po hanggang ngayon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Pero consultant, kailan po kayo naging consultant or trainer ng AMLOC ng PAGCOR?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: 2019 po sa AMLOC, PAGCOR, if I remember it right, Your Honor, 2023 or 2022.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Sa CESA po, kailan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Around that same year po, 2022, 2023.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Sa Aurora Pacific Economic Zone.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Same year, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Matanong ko lamang po. Bakit po parang hindi kayo tumatagal sa isang trabaho? I mean, BIR is good agency.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: GOCC also. Maganda po ang sweldo roon. Commission on Election, lalo na po. Lalo ng Anti-Money Laundering Council because you have all the power. Kinakatakutan kayo. Why? Why? Why? Parang pansin ko yung pinakamatagal nyo na three years po sa isang agency. Ano po nangyari? Hindi ko kayo happy sa trabaho nyo. Anong siste?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Number one, Your Honor, sa BIR, I was a working student. I'm on my fourth year. I have to choose. No? Whether I... Continue with my work or focus on my fourth year. Graduating na ako nun. Sa San Pedro kasi yung fourth year, ang mga klase umaga, hindi upang gabi. So I don't want to shortchange the government. Nauubos na ang aking leave. I have to make a decision. Kaya ako umalis kahit malabag sa aking loob. Pangalawa, sa GCG, okay naman po. Now I was offered a position within the late... Chairman Sixto Brillantes to be part of his team. So I took the chance po, after rendering sa GCG, I think, dumatating ho ang punto ng tao na sa tingin niyo tapos na ang inyong mission. So I have to move to another. And I was invited by a friend. So sumama ho ako doon. Sa kumalik ko, nag-expire na kasi ang term ni Chairman Brillantes noong 2015.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: So talaga ho automat. coterminous ang aking posisyon within Chairman Brillantes. Kaya ako yung nag-apply sa AMLAC at awa naman ng Diyos, nakapasok tayo. Now, sabi ko nga kanina, short but meaningful years. Marami kasi talagang trabaho. Nagsisimula ako ng aking pamilya. I have to make time sa binubuo ko ang pamilya. Kaya ito, dream ng bawat abogado, magkaroon ng sariling opisina, makilala. Ininvite ako ng aking kaibigan, sumama ako. Maganda na nga ang compensation eh. Secured na ang aking future sa benepisyo pa lang sa BSP. Pero I still took that chance. So, dumating nga yung mga point na tama ba yung aking desisyon. Pero ito, nandito ako ngayon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Alam mo ho, Ginoong Testigo. Hindi ho, Kung kayo mag-a-apply ng trabaho, dito po ilalagay niyo sa resume. From 2009, naka-apat, limang co-agency po. Hindi mo maganda tignan sa HR po ito. Pag kayo po in-interview. Ang tatanungin mo sa iyo, tinatanong ko bakit ka umalis sa BIR, bakit ka umalis sa GOCC, COMELEC, anti-money laundering Council. Kasi hindi po parang either kayo may problema. Or hindi ho kayo marunong makisama, I don't know.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Ang ganda lahat po, Your Honor, hanggang ngayon, I still maintain good relationship with my former colleagues. So, I don't burn bridges. So, yan ho, no? Naging mga personal ko na ho silang kaibigan. At yung mga dahilan nung aking pag-alis, it's beyond my control. I have to make hard choices, difficult choices.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: And do you think you made the right choice by leaving AMLC?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: I think... Right now, your honor, nung ako'y nagsisimula, mag-isa lang ako sa aking opisina. Hindi ko alam kung saan pupunta ang practice na to. At naniwala ho yung aking mga naging estudyante, naging kliyente. So, I think I'm on the right track. Hindi ko rin ho 'y isipin na ako'y mapupunta dito sa impeachment court.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Kaya nga po, I was asking you kung did you make the right choice? Did you make the right choice?

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Only God knows, your honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Erwin Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you. Thank you. No further questions, presiding officer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Any other senator or judge who wishes to make an introduction? There being none.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Chair, we'll now excuse the witness. Atty. Raynor, maraming salamat po sa inyong panahon. Pasensya. Gayon din po sa pagsagot sa katanungan ng mga magkabilang partido, gayon din ang senator-judges. Thank you for your time and patience, sir. You are excused, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Rainer P. Dela Fuente
turns.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Before we adjourn, the chair is in receipt of subpoenaed documents from the three witnesses of the respondent, Dr. Rodolfo, Ms. Pagayunan, and the representative of Ms. Mendoza from CITEM as earlier indicated by the Chair. Chair instructs that copies of the subpoenaed documents be furnished to the parties so that there will not be any inordinate delay tomorrow whether during direct or cross with respect to the documents that the witness may be confronted with. So ordered.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: What is the pleasure of the lead counsel for the respondent, Attorney Sheila? Anything before we adjourn?

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Good afternoon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Good afternoon.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Just some manifestations, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: After the entire day of hearing and receiving the testimony of our first witness for today and for this week... We have observed that the court and members of this court as well as the prosecution are interested in the proper application of Article 7, Section 13. And so, since this court may take mandatory judicial notice of Supreme Court decisions as well as decisions of the Sandigan Bayan in criminal cases acquitting the accused charging.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Individuals with purported violations of this provision in relation to RA 6713 or the Code of Ethical Conduct for Public Officers and Employees. We would like to direct the attention of this Court to the following provisions of the law.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: Generally, divestment and conflict of interest are defined under sections 3, paragraph I of Republic Act 6713. Divestment is defined under Section 3, paragraph K of the same law. And in relation to that, the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act 6713 under Rule 7 provides for the contents of SAL and under Section 1, paragraph A, subparagraph. Subparagraph 1 and Section 1, Subparagraph A, Subparagraph 2 provides for a disclosure of business interests and financial connections in relation to the requirement under Section 13, Article 7 of the 1987 Constitution. Now, in relation to that also, we have Rule 9 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 6713 providing actually and explicitly providing For the elements of conflict of interest to arise and the necessity of divestment. In fact, this is provided under Section 1, Subparagraph B of Rule 9 of RA 6713, Implementing Rules and Regulations. And I will read just for the record and so that the public may also hear. Under Section 1, Subparagraph B, conflict of interest occurs When the official or employee is a substantial stockholder or a member of the board of directors or an officer of the corporation or an owner or has substantial interest in a business or a partner in a partnership and number two, the interest of such corporation or business or his rights or duties therein are opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty. Now, with respect to that conflict of interest, the said implementing rules and regulations, meaning the law, provides that under Section 2, subparagraph B, divestment is mandatory only if all the conditions in Section 1, subparagraph B, All the elements enumerated under the preceding paragraph must first concur before the public official or employee may be required to divest himself of such financial or alleged financial interest in any firm or company. Now, I will be citing two Supreme Court decisions which form part of the law of the land. These are, the first one is Trieste. Sr. v. Sandigan Bayan, GR number L-70332-43. This was decided by the Supreme Court on November 13, 1986. And the Court said in that decision of Trieste that what is contemplated in Section 3, Paragraph H of the Antigraph Law is the actual intervention in the transaction. In which one has financial or pecuniary interests in order that liability may attach. And the official... May I just finish, Your Honor? I will also listen to the good prosecutor after I'm done.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: The

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: official

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: need

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: not...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: To continue.

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: The official need not dispose his shares in the corporation as long as he does not do... Anything for the firm in its contract with the office. For the law aims to prevent the use of influence, authority, and power. And the court cited the deliberations on Senate Bill 293, May 6, 1959. This is part of the Congressional Record, Volume 2, page 603, as well as page 604 of the Congressional Record, May 9, 1959. Now, more recently, in 2007,

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison
turns.text: The Supreme Court also rendered a decision in Caballero v. Sandigan Bayan. It reiterated the Trieste ruling that what is contemplated in the law is the actual intervention in the transaction in which one has financial or pecuniary interest in order that liability may attach. And finally, we also found a decision In People v. Dimaala of the Sandigan Bayan, where the prosecution witness was the presiding justice or chairperson of the 3rd Division that acquitted the accused in that case, criminal cases numbers 27, 208, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 23, 24-28 in an amended decision dated June 22, 2018, Your Honor. That's the gist of my manifestation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Court takes judicial notice of the law cited as well as the decision cited which form part of the law of the land. Yes, Honorable Ridon, you are entitled to your own manifestation.

turns.speaker: Rep. Terry L. Ridon
turns.text: No, we will not make a manifestation, Your Honor. I think that is a proper subject of a written memorandum or closing arguments, but we will respect their time that they had spent on the matter. Thank you. We will move forward, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Thank you for your magnanimity. Honorable Ridon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis "Chiz" G. Escudero
turns.text: Maybe I may ask, Attorney Sheila, we have three witnesses for tomorrow. Dr. Rodolfo, Ms. Pagayunan, and the replacement of Ms. Mendoza, correct?

turns.text: In that order?

turns.speaker: Atty. Sheila C. Sison

And since this is a matter for a mandatory judicial notice, Your Honor, motion is not needed, Your Honor.
